title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:04PM by PIB Delhi Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), a constituent unit of Department of Atomic Energy (DAE), has developed 72 improved varieties in different crops using radiation-induced mutagenesis along with cross breeding. These varieties have been released and notified for commercial cultivation across the country in collaboration with Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and State Agricultural Universities (SAUs). These include 17 varieties in groundnut, 10 varieties in rice, 9 varieties each in mungbean and mustard, 8 varieties in urdbean, 5 varieties in pigeonpea, 3 varieties in sorghum, 2 varieties each in cowpea, wheat and soybean, one variety each in banana, sesame, linseed, sunflower and jute. Some of the desirable traits in these crops include higher yield, seed size, early maturity, climate resilient traits like drought, heat, salinity tolerance and resistance to diseases. Several of these varieties have high patronage from the farming community and are extensively grown in the country. Genetic modifications induced through radiations in the different crops do not cause adverse effects. Prior to release, the developed varieties are thoroughly tested through multi-location evaluations over the years and released for commercial cultivation after attaining the superiority over the existing cultivars. DAE has undertaken various initiatives to promote the adoption of improved crop varieties in the Indian farming communities. The steps include, large-scale quality seed production of Trombay varieties along with several state agricultural universities (SAUs) and supply to State seed corporation, ii. State agricultural departments, National Institutes, State agricultural Universities, v. Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs), vii. Farmer cooperatives, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), Seed companies and x. Farmers in several States In addition, DAE has participated in Kisan Melas, Field days, provided technical guidance and training on cultivation practices, conducted exhibitions in different states in collaboration with SAUs. DAE has also conducted Outreach programmes, field demonstrations, distributed seed minikits of the improved Trombay varieties and conducted Public Awareness Programmes on Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy to render benefit to hundreds of farmers. DAE has developed radiation-based food preservation and food processing technologies to reduce the post harvesting losses and extend shelf life of agri products. Also, radiation-based protocols have also been developed for various agricultural products like vegetables, fruits, pulses, spices etc. The technology has been transferred to private entrepreneurs on non-exclusive basis, for commercialization and can be implemented through licensees. Further, Government has implemented policy measures to expand the radiation technology for food preservation at the country level. Government of India has announced incentives for setting up of multiproduct food irradiation units under ‘Integrated Cold Chain & Value Addition Infrastructure’ of the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojana (PMKSY) scheme across the Nation in 2024-25. This scheme is open for application by the interested stakeholders. In the state of Uttar Pradesh, three food irradiation facilities have been commissioned till date in the private sector. In agriculture, DAE has been consistently evaluating their developed breeding lines/mutants in different crops and their release in different agro-climatic zones in respective states in collaboration with State Agricultural Universities (SAU) and various ICAR institutes. DAE has research collaborations and Memorandum of Understandings (MoUs) with the State Agricultural Universities in Assam, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and following ICAR institutes: ICAR - Indian Institute of Groundnut Research, Junagadh ICAR-National Soybean Research Institute, Indore ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed Mustard Research, Bharatpur ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Kanpur and ICAR-National Research Centre for Banana, Trichy. Department also funds several research projects on mutation breeding and food preservation through Board of Research in Nuclear Sciences (BRNS) projects, an Advisory Body of DAE. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298192) आगंतुक पटल  : 94 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: APPLICATION OF RADIATION TECHNOLOGIES FOR AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SECURITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: DOMESTIC SELF-SUFFICIENCY IN CRITICAL MEDICAL RADIOISOTOPE SUPPLY
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Department of Atomic Energy PARLIAMENT QUESTION: DOMESTIC SELF-SUFFICIENCY IN CRITICAL MEDICAL RADIOISOTOPE SUPPLY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:03PM by PIB Delhi Molybdenum-99 (Mo-99), Iodine-131(I-131) and Lutetium-177 (Lu-177) are the most important reactor-produced medical radioisotopes, accounting for nearly 90% of all Nuclear Medicine applications. Owing to their relatively short half-lives, these medical radioisotopes are produced at regular intervals, typically on a weekly or fortnightly basis in the Dhruva reactor, Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC). The total activity of 99 Mo, 131 I and 177 Lu based radiopharmaceutical products produced and supplied during the past five years is detailed below. title: Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare Over 50,000 Saplings Planted Across 31 States on Hariyali Amavasya Under Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative Vriksh Mitra Parivar Drives Nationwide Plantation Campaign Under PM Modi’s ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ Call Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Leads Major Tree Plantation Drive in Delhi on Hariyali Amavasya Vriksh Mitra Parivar Emerges as the Face of a Nationwide Green Movement Planting Trees Means Securing the Future: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Respect for Nature Is the Best Way to Protect Future Generations; The Real Commitment Is to Save Trees, Not Just Plant Them: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan Delhi Has Learnt Much from Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan’s Green Initiative, Says Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa Development Must Go Hand in Hand with Environmental Protection, Says Minister Shri Parvesh Verma प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:34PM by PIB Delhi More than 50,000 saplings were planted across 31 states on the occasion of Hariyali Amavasya as part of a nationwide plantation drive led by Union Minister for Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare and Rural Development Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan in collaboration with the “Vriksh Mitra Parivar.” The campaign drew further momentum from Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative. The program was held at the PBG Ground, Central Ridge, near Talkatora Stadium in New Delhi, where ministers, Members of Parliament, government officials, farmers, youth and citizens participated in the plantation drive. The program began with the watering of saplings and the singing of Vande Mataram, followed by mass plantation. Similar plantation drives were organised across villages, towns, panchayats and institutions in different parts of the country. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar played a key role in mobilising citizens and encouraging them to plant at least one tree. Addressing the gathering, Shri Chouhan said Hariyali Amavasya is not only a religious occasion but also an opportunity to express gratitude towards nature. He said Indian traditions view human beings, animals, birds, rivers, mountains and trees as interconnected elements of the natural ecosystem. “Planting a tree is not just about adding greenery; it is an investment in the future of coming generations,” Shri Chouhan said, stressing that planting saplings must be accompanied by a commitment to their protection and regular care. The Union Minister urged every citizen to plant at least one tree each year and encourage five others to join the campaign. He suggested observing birthdays, wedding anniversaries, the birth of children and the death anniversaries of parents as “Vriksh Parv” by planting trees. Shri Chouhan also called upon panchayats, urban local bodies and institutions to identify designated areas for plantation so that saplings can be protected and maintained over the long term. Highlighting the close link between environmental sustainability and agriculture, Shri Chouhan said environmental degradation directly affects farming, water availability, soil health and human well-being. He said that for farmers, access to water and maintaining soil health are as important as the availability of seeds and fertilisers. He called for greater adoption of Mission LiFE, energy conservation and reduced dependence on plastic to strengthen environmental protection. “Nature must not be exploited; its resources must be used responsibly and conserved for the future,” he said. Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the Delhi Government had drawn valuable lessons from Shri Chouhan’s initiative. He said more than one lakh people in Delhi have been connected with the campaign, while schools, colleges and other institutions are also being encouraged to participate in plantation activities. Shri Sirsa said citizens are increasingly coming forward to take a collective pledge for environmental protection and contribute to the plantation drive. Delhi government's Cabinet Minister Shri Parvesh Verma said the “Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam” initiative should inspire every citizen to take responsibility for protecting the environment. He said development and environmental conservation must go hand in hand, adding that sustainable development requires a balance between infrastructure expansion and preservation of green cover. The program was attended by Member of Parliament Shri Darshan Singh Choudhary, representatives of various institutions, officials from agricultural universities, personnel from ICAR, DARE and KVKs, and a large number of members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar. The nationwide drive was positioned as a tree plantation exercise as well as an effort to build sustained public participation in environmental conservation. The campaign emphasised that planting a sapling is only the first step, while ensuring its survival and growth is an equally important responsibility. Members of the Vriksh Mitra Parivar are continuing to take this message to communities across the country. ***** RC/MS/HR/DK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298322) आगंतुक पटल  : 124 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Agriculture &

title: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Commerce & Industry Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global Nine Free Trade Agreements Open New Market Opportunities for Indian Industry and Businesses: Shri Goyal India’s $30 Trillion Economy Vision by 2047 Presents Major Opportunities for Businesses: Shri Goyal प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:26PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal urged Indian businesses and citizens to adopt fair trading practices, promote recycling and reuse, and encourage a circular economy while taking Indian products and services to global markets. Addressing the inaugural ceremony of the Bharatiya Vyapar Mahotsav at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, Shri Goyal highlighted India’s growing global economic engagement and noted that markets have been opened for Indian industry and businesses through nine free trade agreements. He said that international trade now provides India preferential access and highlighted the contribution of Indian MSMEs, employees, fishermen, farmers, entrepreneurs and the services sector in taking Indian products and services to global markets. Shri Goyal called for collective efforts to strengthen the Make in India brand by respecting India’s quality, design capabilities and brand. He said that India’s current economic size of around $4 trillion presents a major opportunity as the country moves towards the vision of becoming a $30 trillion economy by 2047. He noted that the whole world is seeking to increase trade relations with India and emphasised that such a large growth opportunity requires collective participation from businesses, entrepreneurs and citizens. The Minister noted the growth of India’s exports and said that goods and services exports reached a record level of 863 trillion dollars last year, comprising 442 trillion dollars of merchandise exports and 421 trillion dollars of services exports. He said that exports had registered around 73 per cent growth over the last six years and that the target for the current year is to achieve exports of 1 trillion dollars. He further noted that exports recorded almost 15 per cent growth during the first four months from April to July of the current year. Shri Goyal emphasised that self-reliance and national development go hand in hand. He said that citizens must themselves become part of the change and contribute to the country’s journey towards self-reliance. He highlighted various initiatives undertaken since 2014, including Digital India, Startup India, Stand-Up India and large-scale infrastructure development, which have contributed to strengthening industry and business and creating opportunities for the youth. He said that ‘Swadeshi’ represents products made in India with the blood, sweat and tears of Indian citizens. He called upon Indian businesses to move beyond limited markets and take local products and services to global markets. He said that greater participation of Indian consumers in Indian products would create new opportunities, increase production and trade, enable economies of scale and make Indian businesses more competitive. The Minister said that the people of India have demonstrated their capability to convert challenges into opportunities and emerge stronger. He highlighted the collective strength of travellers, MSMEs, startups, farmers, fishermen, labourers and entrepreneurs and said that this strength would help India take its products and services to the world. Calling for greater participation in the country’s development journey, Shri Goyal said that the reform process involves improvement, transformation and performance, and that all stakeholders have a responsibility to demonstrate their capabilities and take India to the world through their work. Shri Goyal called upon businesses and entrepreneurs to digitise their businesses, adopt good manufacturing practices and follow fair trading practices. He emphasised the importance of sustainability in the context of climate change and called for greater focus on recycling, reuse and a circular economy. The Minister said that India’s journey should not only give a label to Make in India but also establish respect for India’s quality, design capabilities and brand. He expressed confidence that Indian products and natural resources would become trusted globally through these collective efforts. Shri Goyal also said that growth in GDP would naturally lead to higher production and create employment opportunities. He noted that young people returning to India after completing their education or acquiring new skills through skill development centres would bring new solutions to address emerging challenges. He emphasised that the collective efforts of Indian businesses, entrepreneurs, MSMEs, farmers, fishermen and workers would contribute to the country’s growth and help India emerge as a stronger participant in the global economy. *** Abhishek Dayal/Abhijith Narayanan/Anushka Pandey (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298156) आगंतुक पटल  : 291 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , Marathi , हिन्दी , Bengali , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Commerce & Industry Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal Calls for Fair Trading Practices and Taking ‘Make in India’ from Local to Global Nine Free Trade Agreements Open New Market Opportunities for Indian Industry and Businesses: Shri Goyal India’s $30 Trillion Economy Vision by 2047 Presents Major Opportunities for Businesses: Shri Goyal प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Three Sanchar Mitras Selected as ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Three Sanchar Mitras Selected as ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030 Recognition highlights growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 7:27PM by PIB Delhi With an objective of creating opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future at the international level, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Government of India, has facilitated the selection of three Sanchar Mitras (youth volunteers) from India as Generation Connect Youth Envoys (GCYE) of the International Telecommunication Union (ITU). This comes as the global community celebrates International Youth Day 2026 under the theme “ Different Contexts, Common Aspirations ”. The Generation Connect community marked the occasion through the virtual “Passing the Torch: Connecting Generations of Digital Leaders” event today , bringing together the outgoing and incoming cohorts of Generation Connect Youth Envoys. Ankit Kumar Pal from Delhi, Manish Kumar Mandal from Bengaluru and Susmita Sain from Guwahati have been selected as part of the third cohort of ITU Generation Connect Youth Envoys for the period 2026–2030 in recognition of their contribution under the Sanchar Mitra scheme of DoT. Their selection marks an important recognition of the growing role of Indian youth in shaping the global digital future. The Generation Connect Youth Envoys programme provides young people with opportunities to contribute to national, regional and global discussions and initiatives related to Information and Communication Technologies (ICTs), digital transformation and inclusive digital development. The initiative aligns closely with the objectives of the Sanchar Mitra Scheme, which seeks to engage young people in telecom and digital initiatives and provide them exposure to national and international platforms. The scheme also envisages opportunities for selected Sanchar Mitras to participate in global telecom platforms such as the ITU. Following ITU’s invitation for nominations to the third cohort of Generation Connect Youth Envoys, the Department of Telecommunications initiated a process to identify suitable candidates from among Sanchar Mitras. The process sought candidates with demonstrated engagement in areas including youth-led initiatives, digital inclusion, ICT education and skills, research and technical activities, entrepreneurship and innovation, and community-level ICT initiatives. The recognition also reflects India’s commitment to empowering young people as active contributors to the country’s digital transformation journey and strengthening youth participation in global conversations on technology, connectivity and inclusive digital development. Through initiatives such as Sanchar Mitra and its engagement with global platforms including the ITU Generation Connect programme, the Department of Telecommunications continues to create opportunities for India’s youth to learn, participate, lead and contribute to the evolving digital future. About Sanchar Mitra The Sanchar Mitra Scheme envisions to engage the Yuva Shakti- India’s youth, as catalysts for digital empowerment and societal outreach. The students nominated as Sanchar Mitra actively conduct awareness drives in communities, educational institutions, public spaces, etc., focusing on key telecom-related issues, like citizen-centric telecom services, prevention of telecom frauds and mobile security - promoting digital safety, and foster responsible telecom usage. This scheme is open to students from those technical institutes that have active telecom, electronics, computers, cybersecurity or similar programs and have agreed to participate in the scheme. The scheme has been implemented across all states/ UTs through the LSA field offices of DoT. More than 200 institutions are currently participating in it. title: The Government of India to launch the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the Union Territories of Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Company Affairs The Government of India to launch the Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC)-based Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) in the Union Territories of Chandigarh and Dadra & Nagar Haveli प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation BHARAT TAXI ROLL OUT प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi Bharat Taxi, a cooperative-led digital App mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), a multistate cooperative society is officially launched in the cities of Delhi-NCR, Gujarat, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The implementation of Bharat Taxi Services is being carried out in a phased manner across the country. The implementation includes registration and onboarding of Sarathis (drivers), customer enrolment, training programmes and expansion of services to identified cities and States. As on 04.08.2026, the platform has registered 8.48 lakh Sarathis (drivers) and 44.27 lakh customers. The platform is facilitating 11,106 daily rides and has enabled cumulative earnings of ₹83.70 crore for Sarathis. The rollout of services of Bharat Taxi, operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), in other cities and States is subject to operational requirements and necessary approvals. Expansion is undertaken based on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions, and other stakeholders. The details of operation of Bharat Taxi in various cities and average daily rides, as on 04.08.2026, are as under: City Average Daily rides Delhi- NCR 5574 Gujarat 3817 Lucknow 324 Chandigarh 190 Mumbai 197 Jaipur 372 Pune 632 Total 11,106 . Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi are separate mobility platforms operating under different institutional frameworks. Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-based mobility platform operated by Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL) under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, whereas Yatri Sathi is a mobility platform developed and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics (DITE), Government of West Bengal. On 19th July, 2026, STCL entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Government of West Bengal for collaboration with the Yatri Sathi platform. Under the MoU, Bharat Taxi extends support in the areas of driver enrolment, cooperative membership, driver welfare and public outreach. title: AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:12PM by PIB Delhi Ministry of Cooperation has set up Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies (MSCS) Act, 2002 to act as an apex organization for production, procurement, processing, branding, labelling, packaging, storage, marketing, distribution and strategic research & development of quality seeds with a clear vision to build a strong, farmer-centric seed system through a cooperative-led structure. Bhartiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has so far introduced seeds of 18 crops and 124 varieties in the market under the 'Bharat Beej' brand for distribution across the country. Further, BBSSL has undertaken initiatives for developing production and quality-testing requirements for vegetable seeds in accordance with the prescribed seed quality and regulatory standards. During the financial year 2025–26, BBSSL produced 75,535 metric tonnes of seeds through its associated seed-producing farmers under the seed production programme for the 'Bharat Beej' brand. The programme facilitates farmers' participation in organised seed production and provides technical support for the production of seeds in accordance with the prescribed quality and certification standards. For the conservation of traditional indigenous varieties, BBSSL has initiated a programme in Uttarakhand focusing on the identification, conservation, multiplication and documentation of such varieties. BBSSL's activities include the expansion of domestic seed production, conservation of indigenous genetic resources, and distribution of quality seeds through the cooperative network, thereby contributing to the objective of reducing the country's dependence on imported seeds and strengthening self-reliance in the seed sector. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298385) आगंतुक पटल  : 87 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation AVAILABILITY OF QUALITY SEEDS AND FARMERS' SELF-RELIANCE THROUGH BBSSL प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:10PM by PIB Delhi Using the National Cooperative Database (NCD), a ranking framework has been introduced to rank the primary cooperative societies, sector wise and State / district / block wise. The Ranking Framework was launched on 24.01.2025. It enables the Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS) of State / UT to generate rankings of primary cooperative societies of 12 sectors through the NCD portal. This Ranking Framework helps to enhance transparency, efficiency, and effectiveness within the societies, while also improving their credibility and competitive capability. The ranking framework enables State/ UT RCS to assess the performance of cooperative societies based on five broad categories / parameters, namely audit compliance, operational activities, financial performance, infrastructure, and basic identity information. Under the Ranking Framework, weightage scores have generally been assigned to these categories in the aforesaid order, with an overall weightage of 100 marks. The Cooperative Ranking Framework is an important step towards strengthening the cooperative sector, providing cooperatives with actionable insights, benchmarks for performance, and an opportunity to foster competition and innovation. This ranking framework can be used for dissemination of best practices of the top-performing cooperative societies in each sector, so that other societies can learn and adopt these best practices. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298378) आगंतुक पटल  : 48 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation OBJECTIVE OF THE RANKING FRAMEWORK FOR COOPERATIVE SOCIETIES प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) markets its certified organic products under the "Bharat Organics" brand through a multi-channel marketing strategy. Its products are marketed via various e-commerce platforms, modern retail chains, cooperative outlets including Safal/Mother Dairy, NAFED, NCCF, etc., and its Direct-to-Consumer (D2C) portal. The benchmark for organic production in India is the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP), which is notified by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) complies with these benchmarks by procuring and marketing only certified organic products that conform to NPOP standards. The products are sourced from valid certified farmer groups, Internal Control Systems (ICS), or certified operators and are subject to stringent quality testing, traceability mechanisms, and compliance with applicable food safety and organic certification requirements. In addition, NCOL ensures mandatory laboratory testing of organic produce for pesticide residues and other quality parameters before marketing, thereby maintaining the prescribed standards for organic production in India. NCOL promotes the formation of National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)-certified Internal Control System (ICS) groups through cooperative societies to support organic farmers. It facilitates the procurement of certified organic produce through cooperative societies at fair and transparent prices and markets organic products under the Bharat Organics brand through multiple sales channels. NCOL has signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with 28 States/UTs to promote the organic cooperative ecosystem and facilitate greater participation of farmers in organic farming. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298375) आगंतुक पटल  : 53 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation BENCHMARKS FOR ORGANIC PRODUCTS OF NCOL प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation DIGITAL TECHNOLOGY IN THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:04PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Cooperation has undertaken several reformative measures during the last three years to promote digital technology, transparency and good governance in the cooperative sector under the vision of "Sahkar Se Samriddhi" . The major initiatives and their outcomes are as under:- Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project: The Ministry is implementing the Centrally Sponsored Project for Computerisation of functional PACS with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 Crore which has now been increased up to 2925.39 Crore which entails bringing all the functional PACS onto an ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based common national software, linking them with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). This has been done with a view to improving their operational efficiency, transparency and accountability through ERP-based National Software. The project facilitates standardized accounting, audit, MIS, online service delivery and integration with various national digital platforms, thereby enabling efficient governance and better service delivery to members. Under the Computerisation of Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) Project, 63,686 PACS have been onboarded on the ERP-based National Software, 54,707 PACS have been declared as e-PACS and more than 51.58 crore digital transactions have been carried out through the software as on 15.07.2026 , leading to enhanced transparency, improved service delivery and better financial management at the grassroots level. To promote digital technology and transparency, the ePACS software includes the following features: Comprehensive functional coverage: The software comprises 22 ERP modules covering the entire spectrum of PACS operations, including credit (loan origination, sanction, disbursement and recovery), deposits, accounting, audit, member management, procurement and other business functions of PACS. Standardised, CAS-MIS compliant accounting: The software generates books of accounts and financial statements in conformity with the Common Accounting System and Management Information System (CAS-MIS) norms, thereby bringing uniformity in accounting practices across PACS in the country. Interoperability and integration: The software supports integration with Aadhaar-enabled services, Core Banking Systems (CBS) of StCBs/DCCBs, Point of Sale (PoS) devices, Common Service Centres (CSC), the National Cooperative Database (NCD) and State-specific portals, enabling PACS to function as part of a larger digital ecosystem. Digital credit delivery: The software provides facilities such as end-to-end loan origination, KCC processing and mobile application support, facilitating faster and more transparent credit delivery to members. Secure cloud architecture: Data of all onboarded PACS is maintained on secure, centralised cloud-based storage with appropriate cyber security safeguards, dispensing with dependence on standalone local systems and physical records. Internal controls and on-system audit: The software incorporates maker-checker functionality and an on-system audit module, enabling continuous monitoring of transactions and conduct of statutory audit directly on the system. Dashboards, analytics and MIS: Dashboards, analytics and MIS reports are available to higher-tier stakeholders for monitoring and decision support. Multi-lingual capability: A key feature of the software is its multi-lingual capability, which enables PACS personnel to operate the software in regional languages. At present, the software is available in 20 languages. State-specific customisation: While the core software is common across the country, it is customisable to accommodate State-specific bye-laws, products, processes and reporting requirements. Till date, loan details of 4.02 crore borrowers of PACS, amounting to ₹2.3 lakh crore , have been digitised and are available to authorised stakeholders on ePACS. Deposit details of 5.49 crore depositors , amounting to about ₹37,000 crore , have also been digitised. Membership records of 10.30 crore members are now available on ePACS. These PACS-wise, member-wise records, which were hitherto available only through physical access, are now on ePACS. The CSC portal has been integrated with ePACS, enabling PACS to function as Common Service Centres and offer citizen-centric services. Integration with PMKSK, AgriStack and PMBJK are at advanced stages. NABARD is in the process of implementing end-to-end digitisation of the loan process through ePACS, followed by integration with the Krishi Rin Portal (KRP), to ensure efficient loan sanction and disbursement as well as targeted delivery of interest subvention benefits to members. Through integration with the AgriStack portal, the farmer profile, land and crop details of farmers, as well as Scale of Finance (SoF) details, can be utilised for processing and sanctioning loans in the ePACS system. Further, the details of loans sanctioned through ePACS will be shared with KRP using Aadhaar as the common identifier, ensuring that interest subvention benefits are directed to loanees on an Aadhaar-authenticated basis. A phased implementation strategy is also followed for integrating ePACS with the Core Banking Solutions (CBS) of DCCBs to enable both seven-day loan disbursal and the “paperless to cashless” goal. As this integration entails work at both the ePACS and the CBS levels, the CBS vendors of DCCBs are also required to participate in the process. The initial focus is on the TCS vendor, which covers 168 banks (StCBs/DCCBs) across 16 States, and the integration will subsequently be extended to other CBS vendors. Maker-checker controls: The software provides maker-checker functionality, whereby transactions are subjected to multiple levels of verification before authorisation, thereby strengthening internal controls and reducing operational risks. Computerisation of the Office of Registrar of Cooperative Societies (RCS): Centrally sponsored project for computerization of RCS offices in States/Union Territories has been launched by the Ministry on 30.01.2024 with a budgetary outlay of Rs.94.59 crore for three years w.e.f. 2023-24. This is a part of the umbrella project of “Strengthening Cooperatives Through IT Interventions” of the Ministry. Further, GOI share amounting to Rs 16.74 crore has been released to 10 States/UTs in FY 2023-24, FY 24-25, FY 2025-26 and FY 2026-27 for procurement of hardware, digitization, and setting up of support systems . Till date, 9 States/UTs have procured the Hardware under the project. Outcome: A more data-driven, forward-looking and risk-sensitive supervisory ecosystem for the cooperative sector. Model policies aligned with RBI Master Directions NABARD has initiated development of 26 model policies covering governance, IT, cyber security, audit, compliance and risk management, aligned with RBI's consolidated Master Directions, for uniform adoption by RCBs. The reformative measures undertaken by the Ministry have significantly strengthened digital technology adoption, transparency and good governance in the cooperative sector. These initiatives have enabled digitization of cooperative institutions through ERP-based software, standardized accounting systems, digital record management, online monitoring, audit trails and real-time Management Information Systems (MIS), resulting in improved operational efficiency, transparency and accountability. Overall, these digital interventions have promoted transparency, accountability, evidence-based decision-making and efficient governance, while facilitating better delivery of services to cooperative societies and their members across the country. title: COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:03PM by PIB Delhi Several State-level Cooperative Federations are engaged in activities related to organic farming, procurement, processing, branding, marketing, and promotion of organic products in their respective States. National Cooperative Organics Limited (NCOL) coordinates with State Cooperative Federations through various measures, including entering into Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), as appropriate, with State Cooperative Departments/Nodal Agencies for promoting certified organic farming, procurement and marketing. It also associates State Cooperative Federations, Cooperative Societies, Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) and other cooperative institutions as members/partners to facilitate their participation in the organic value chain, including aggregation, procurement, processing, packaging and marketing of organic produce under the "Bharat Organics" brand. In addition, NCOL facilitates the formation of National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)-certified Internal Control System (ICS) groups through cooperative institutions. This information was given by Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation, Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298366) आगंतुक पटल  : 37 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation COORDINATION BETWEEN NCOL AND STATE COOPERATIVE FEDERATIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Corporate Affairs National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) today launched its e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services. Hon’ble President, NCLT, Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, inaugurated the services through video conferencing, marking another step towards making the Tribunal’s Registry more accessible and technology-enabled. Speaking on the occasion, Justice Grewal said that the two services are intended to provide advocates, litigants and other stakeholders with convenient and faster access to judicial records and certified copies. The services form part of the Tribunal’s broader digital transformation, including the revamped NCLT website and the ongoing e-Courts 2.0 initiative. The Hon’ble NCLT President also highlighted the measures undertaken to improve case management and reduce pendency. The NCLT has adopted a data-driven mechanism to monitor pendency across Benches. Based on the data so collated, workload was reviewed and redistributed, Special Benches were constituted wherever required, and efforts were made to maximise the available Court time. These measures contributed to the approval of 78 resolution plans during April–June 2026, the highest first-quarter performance since the enactment of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, involving approximately ₹5,517.66 crore. The NCLT has also issued detailed guidelines on registration and listing of cases, in consultation with the Bar, to ensure optimum utilisation of limited judicial resources. Justice Grewal emphasised that while the Tribunal continues to face infrastructural and manpower constraints, sustained efforts are being made to reduce avoidable delays and improve efficiency. The launch of the two services is part of the NCLT’s continuing endeavour to provide a more transparent, efficient and stakeholder-oriented system of justice delivery. **** SR/ONP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298542) आगंतुक पटल  : 52 Ministry of Corporate Affairs National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) Launches e-Inspection and e-Certified Copy Services प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flags off ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026’ dedicated to National Song Vande Mataram, today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Culture Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan flags off ‘Har Ghar Tiranga Bike Rally 2026’ dedicated to National Song Vande Mataram, today at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi Union Ministers and Members of Parliament join the patriotic bike rally at Delhi प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:38PM by PIB Delhi A grand Tiranga Bike Rally 2026 was flagged off from Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today as part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 , dedicated to the National Song Vande Mataram . Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, flagged off the rally in the presence of Union Cabinet Ministers including Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, Shri Kiren Rijiju, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Union Minister of Minority Affairs; Shri G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister of Coal and Mines; Dr. Virendra Kumar, Union Minister of Social Justice and Empowerment; Dr. Jitendra Singh, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences and Union Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office; Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh, Union Minister of Panchayati Raj and Union Minister of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying; Union Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, Smt. Nimuben Bambhaniya; Shri Rao Inderjit Singh, Union Minister of state for Culture and Union Minister of state (Independent Charge) of Statistics, Programme Implementation and Planning; Shri V. Somanna, Union Minister of State in the Ministry of Railways; and Union Ministers of State for Home Affairs, Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar and Shri Nityanand Rai and several Members of Parliament. While addressing the gathering Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan expressed deep emotion on the historic occasion of commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. He stated that these two immortal words had awakened a burning spirit of patriotism in the hearts and minds of Indians during the struggle to free the Motherland from British colonial rule. He observed that no other expression had captured the awakening of a nation with such power and resonance. Recalling that Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay had penned these immortal words, he said that they gave voice to the very soul of the nation. Vice-President further highlighted that while people had once marched for the independence of the nation, India was now witnessing a confident and resurgent Bharat marching towards the mission set by the Prime Minister for the Viksit Bharat by 2047. He urged everyone to carry this spirit forward by actively promoting the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign in their respective constituencies, states, streets and homes. He concluded by emphasising that as the wheels began to turn, the journey should not end with the rally, and that the spirit of Vande Mataram should remain alive beyond the celebration. Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, in his welcome address stated that the gathering was not merely for a bike rally, but was an expression of respect and support for the Tiranga, the symbol of India’s independence and an emblem that binds the nation together in one thread. He recalled that nearly five years ago, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi had set before the nation the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047. He further noted that even before the beginning of the Amrit Kaal of independence, the Prime Minister had envisioned such Tiranga yatras across the country. The rally also witnessed enthusiastic participation from over 350 CAPF bikers which included CRPF, BSF, Assam Riffles among other. Over 50 Special biker groups and women bikers also participated in the rally. As part of the ongoing Har Ghar Tiranga 2026 campaign, dedicated to the spirit of national song Vande Mataram, citizens are encouraged to hoist the National Flag at their homes and workplaces between 9 and 17 August and actively participate in this nationwide celebration of patriotism and national unity. *** M Annadurai (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298167) आगंतुक पटल  : 162 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Tamil , Kannada Ministry of Culture Vice-President Shri C. title: Parliament Question: IGB Meeting Of BRICS Network University
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: IGB Meeting Of BRICS Network University प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:38PM by PIB Delhi During India’s BRICS Chairship 2026, the Ministry of Education organized the BRICS  Network University (BRICS NU) conference, virtually, on 20 th July 2026. The theme of the meeting was "Need and Challenges of Preservation of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems in the  Digital Age". The Conference was divided into three sessions - (i) Mapping, Identification and Systematic Documentation of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems across BRICS  Countries, (ii) Preservation and Protection of Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems and  (iii) Role of Digital Technologies in Preserving Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems. During these sessions, subject experts from India and BRICS member countries held deliberations on mapping, identification, systematic documentation, preservation, protection and using digital technologies in preserving traditional and indigenous knowledge systems. India shared the  “Guiding Principles on Strengthening Collaboration on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge System” with the member countries of BRICS. The International Governing Board Meeting (IGB) of the BRICS NU took place, virtually, on 21 st July 2026. During the meeting, members of the IGB presented updates on the collaborative activities among the 178 participating universities across 11 International Thematic Groups (ITGs) in the BRICS NU. Under the BRICS NU, each BRICS Member Country has the option to nominate two Higher Educational Institutes which work on subjects of focus in 11 International Thematic Groups (ITGs). India has 22 Institutions within the BRICS NU. India proposed “Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge System” as the 12 th ITG during the BRICS NU and IGB meetings and has also been mentioned in the Declaration adopted during the 13 th BRICS Education Ministers Meeting on 7 th August 2026. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298515) आगंतुक पटल  : 57 Ministry of Education Parliament Question: IGB Meeting Of BRICS Network University प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Parliament Question: Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has framed and approved the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 to transform the education landscape into a multidisciplinary, inclusive, and learner-centric ecosystem. The Policy aims to enhance equity, quality and access to education for all, while promoting research and innovation as key components of higher education. In pursuance with the vision of NEP 2020, the Ministry of Education has launched the Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme to attract and engage distinguished Indian-origin researchers, scientists and professionals with international research experience, to strengthen India's higher education and research ecosystem through research, mentorship and institutional capacity-building across national priority thematic areas. The Scheme provides for fellowships under three categories, namely Research Chair, Senior Fellow and Young Research Fellow. Under the Scheme, seven institutions have been identified as Lead Institutions. As on date, more than 3,600 applications for fellowship and more than 400 applications from host institutions have been received. The government has made provision of Rs 200 crore for the PMRC Scheme for the year 2026-27. The Scheme envisages India’s position as a global hub of research, innovation and knowledge creation by providing benefits of structured engagement of Indian-origin researchers and scientists to Higher Education Institutions (HEIs), national laboratories, and research centres. Details of scheme, eligibility criteria for fellows and host institutions are available at https://pmrc.education.gov.in/ This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar , in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298511) आगंतुक पटल  : 41 Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Prime Minister Research Chair (PMRC) Scheme 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Parliament Question: Regulation and Oversight of Private Coaching Institution
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Regulation and Oversight of Private Coaching Institution प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:37PM by PIB Delhi Keeping in view the growth in number of unregulated private coaching centres; instances of such centers charging exorbitant fees from students; loss of precious lives due to fire and other accidents; significance of mental well-being; and many malpractices being adopted by these centres, Ministry has circulated Guidelines for Regulation of Coaching Center to States/UTs on 16.01.2024 for taking further action by way of appropriate legal framework. The guidelines for regulation of coaching centres are accessible at https://www.dohe-education.gov.in/documents/acts-and-policies/guidelines-for-regulation-of-coaching-center-ADNyEDOtQWa?pageTitle=Guidelines-for-Regulation-of-Coaching-Center The Guidelines encompass several key aspects, including specifying conditions and necessary documents for registration, issues related to fees, outlining infrastructure prerequisites for establishing coaching centers, establishing a code of conduct for coaching centers; lay emphasis on significance of mental well-being, no batch segregation, maintenance of records, grievance/complaint redressal mechanism etc. The guidelines inter-alia provides for a coaching center to have a website with updated details of the qualification of tutors, details and duration of courses/curriculum, the fees being charged, easy exit policy, fee refund policy, number of students undertaking coaching from the center and number of students who finally succeeded in getting admission in Higher Education Institutions etc. Education is a subject of the Concurrent List and both Central and State governments work collaboratively to provide equitable access to education. After issue of Guidelines by the Central Government, a number of States/UTs have brought out guidelines / regulations / legislations to regulate Private Coaching and tuition classes in their respective states/UTs, such as Andhra Pradesh Coaching Institutions (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2026, the Himachal Pradesh Private Coaching Centres (Registration and Regulation) Rules 2026, Policy and Guidelines for Registration, Control & Regulation of Coaching Institutes in the Union Territory of Puducherry, 2026, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Tamil Nadu Coaching Centres, 2026, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centers in Andaman and Nicobar Islands 2026, the Rajasthan Coaching Centres (Control and Regulation) Act, 2025, Jharkhand Coaching Centre (Control and Regulation), Act 2025, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centers in Tripura, 2025, the Assam Coaching Institutes (Control and Regulation) Act, 2025, Guidelines for Registration and Regulation of Coaching Centres in the State of Nagaland, 2025, Haryana Registration and Regulation of Private Coaching Institutes Act, 2024. Under the provisions of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has also issued comprehensive guidelines on 13.11.2024 to address the issue of misleading advertisements in the coaching sector. These guidelines prohibit coaching centres from making false or misleading claims/advertisements to promote their services and from engaging in deceptive or unfair practices. It also provides that any person who is engaged in coaching shall not use names, photographs, testimonials or videos of successful candidates in an advertisement without the candidate's written consent. The guidelines also regulate unfair contracts and impose strict penalties under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, ensuring accountability and ethical practices in the coaching sector. CCPA imposes penalties on coaching institutes and directs them to discontinue the misleading advertisements and unfair trade practices. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar , in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298513) आगंतुक पटल  : 42 Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Regulation and Oversight of Private Coaching Institution प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Parliament Question: Conduct of CBSE Sports Competitions and Technical Assistance
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Conduct of CBSE Sports Competitions and Technical Assistance प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi CBSE Games are governed by the comprehensive CBSE Games (Guidelines) (available on the CBSE sports portal) and the annual circulars (e.g., Circular No. Acad 19/2026). Key provisions include: Structure: Events are held at Cluster level (broadly state-based; higher-participation games such as Athletics, Basketball, Football (Boys), Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Table  Tennis, Volleyball), Zonal level (for lower-participation games such as Archery,  Badminton, Boxing, Chess, Football (Girls), Handball, Hockey, Judo, Shooting, Skating, Swimming, Taekwondo, Tennis, Yogasana), and National level. Certain  games (Aerobics, Gymnastics, and Rope Skipping) are held directly at National level. Age criteria: Calculated as on 31 December of the year of the event (e.g., for 2026- 27: Under-11 born on/after 01.01.2016; Under-14 on/after 01.01.2013; Under-17  on/after 01.01.2010; Under-19 on/after 01.01.2008). Eligibility and participation: Online registration of students (UID-based),  application to participate, and confirmation to the organising school. The winners of  Cluster/Zonal level competitions qualify for Nationals. Foreign schools compete  under Foreign Zone(s) and qualify directly to Nationals. Organising schools: Selected via online applications, Regional Sports Committee  recommendations, and finalisation by the National Sports Committee. Schools must  have adequate infrastructure (preferably as per SAI specifications) and upload  supporting videos. Other rules: Cover eligibility documents, disqualification, safety measures, accommodation/meals (participants typically pay a prescribed daily charge), certificates (online generation); medals provided by CBSE, and sport-specific rules  (generally aligned with recognised federations/SGFI where applicable). In case of  clash/ambiguity, the latest circular prevails. As per the CBSE Games (Guidelines), the organising school is responsible for hiring technically qualified and experienced umpires/referees/game officials from the District/State Sports Associations/Federations of the concerned game to ensure fair play. CBSE provides a fixed Sports Grant to organising schools (not a variable year-wise budgetary allocation published separately for this purpose). As per the current Guidelines and Circulars (consistent across recent years, including 2023–24, 2024–25 and 2025–26  provisions): Cluster/Zonal level: Rs 2,00,000 National level: Rs 3,00,000 Athletics and Swimming: Rs 4,00,000 (Cluster/Zonal) and Rs 5,00,000 (National). Year Total Grant allotted to schools in र 2023-2024 6,32,00,000 2024-2025 12,13,00,000 2025-2026 9,00,00,000 The grant is to be utilised for the approved heads (payment to referees/ technical  officials/ observers, ground maintenance, sports equipments, tentage, videography,  miscellaneous, etc.). Organising schools must submit expenditure details in the prescribed Proforma along with a Utilisation Certificate certifying that the grant has been fully utilised for the sanctioned purpose. The proforma includes a detailed Statement of Income & Expenditure (covering  accommodation, equipment, first-aid, tentage, referees/officials, ceremonies, photography,  TA/DA to Observer, transport, etc.). The organising schools are required to get the proforma and accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant before uploading on CBSE Integrated Payment System (IPS) portal. CBSE gets these proformas and accounts audited by internal as well as external audit teams. Fair conduct and adherence to rules: Technically qualified officials from the concerned District/State Sports Associations/Federations are hired by the organizing schools to ensure fair play. Grievance/Protest mechanism: Any protest must be submitted in writing to the Organising Secretary within 30 minutes of the declaration of the result, accompanied by a fee  of Rs 1,000. It is considered by the Jury of Appeal. Parties are heard. If the protest is upheld, the fee is refunded; otherwise, it is forfeited. The Jury’s decision is final and binding and is reported (with full facts) to the CBSE Sports Cell. All stakeholders are directed to follow the Rules of Sports & Games , and CBSE Games (Guidelines) available on the CBSE sports portal. Queries may be addressed to the  CBSE Sports Cell (e.g., via the contact details given in the circulars).                         12 AUG 2026 6:36PM by PIB Delhi CBSE Games are governed by the comprehensive CBSE Games (Guidelines) (available on the CBSE sports portal) and the annual circulars (e.g., Circular No. Acad 19/2026). Key provisions include: Structure: Events are held at Cluster level (broadly state-based; higher-participation games such as Athletics, Basketball, Football (Boys), Kabaddi, Kho-Kho, Table  Tennis, Volleyball), Zonal level (for lower-participation games such as Archery,  Badminton, Boxing, Chess, Football (Girls), Handball, Hockey, Judo, Shooting, Skating, Swimming, Taekwondo, Tennis, Yogasana), and National level. Certain  games (Aerobics, Gymnastics, and Rope Skipping) are held directly at National level. Age criteria: Calculated as on 31 December of the year of the event (e.g., for 2026- 27: Under-11 born on/after 01.01.2016; Under-14 on/after 01.01.2013; Under-17  on/after 01.01.2010; Under-19 on/after 01.01.2008). Eligibility and participation: Online registration of students (UID-based),  application to participate, and confirmation to the organising school. The winners of  Cluster/Zonal level competitions qualify for Nationals. Foreign schools compete  under Foreign Zone(s) and qualify directly to Nationals. Organising schools: Selected via online applications, Regional Sports Committee  recommendations, and finalisation by the National Sports Committee. Schools must  have adequate infrastructure (preferably as per SAI specifications) and upload  supporting videos. Other rules: Cover eligibility documents, disqualification, safety measures, accommodation/meals (participants typically pay a prescribed daily charge), certificates (online generation); medals provided by CBSE, and sport-specific rules  (generally aligned with recognised federations/SGFI where applicable). In case of  clash/ambiguity, the latest circular prevails. As per the CBSE Games (Guidelines), the organising school is responsible for hiring technically qualified and experienced umpires/referees/game officials from the District/State Sports Associations/Federations of the concerned game to ensure fair play. CBSE provides a fixed Sports Grant to organising schools (not a variable year-wise budgetary allocation published separately for this purpose). As per the current Guidelines and Circulars (consistent across recent years, including 2023–24, 2024–25 and 2025–26  provisions): Cluster/Zonal level: Rs 2,00,000 National level: Rs 3,00,000 Athletics and Swimming: Rs 4,00,000 (Cluster/Zonal) and Rs 5,00,000 (National). Year Total Grant allotted to schools in र 2023-2024 6,32,00,000 2024-2025 12,13,00,000 2025-2026 9,00,00,000 The grant is to be utilised for the approved heads (payment to referees/ technical  officials/ observers, ground maintenance, sports equipments, tentage, videography,  miscellaneous, etc.). Organising schools must submit expenditure details in the prescribed Proforma along with a Utilisation Certificate certifying that the grant has been fully utilised for the sanctioned purpose. The proforma includes a detailed Statement of Income & Expenditure (covering  accommodation, equipment, first-aid, tentage, referees/officials, ceremonies, photography,  TA/DA to Observer, transport, etc.). The organising schools are required to get the proforma and accounts audited by a Chartered Accountant before uploading on CBSE Integrated Payment System (IPS) portal. CBSE gets these proformas and accounts audited by internal as well as external audit teams. Fair conduct and adherence to rules: Technically qualified officials from the concerned District/State Sports Associations/Federations are hired by the organizing schools to ensure fair play. Grievance/Protest mechanism: Any protest must be submitted in writing to the Organising Secretary within 30 minutes of the declaration of the result, accompanied by a fee  of Rs 1,000. It is considered by the Jury of Appeal. Parties are heard. If the protest is upheld, the fee is refunded; otherwise, it is forfeited. The Jury’s decision is final and binding and is reported (with full facts) to the CBSE Sports Cell. All stakeholders are directed to follow the Rules of Sports & Games , and CBSE Games (Guidelines) available on the CBSE sports portal. Queries may be addressed to the  CBSE Sports Cell (e.g., via the contact details given in the circulars). title: Parliament Question: Foreign University Campuses and Overseas Campuses of Indian Institutions
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Foreign University Campuses and Overseas Campuses of Indian Institutions प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:35PM by PIB Delhi University Grants Commission (UGC) has issued 16 Letters of Intent (LoIs) to Foreign Higher Educational Institutions (FHEIs) from Australia, Italy, United Kingdom and the United States of America. UGC has issued LoIs to six FHEIs in Karnataka, six in Maharashtra, three in Delhi NCR and one in Tamil Nadu. Out of the six LoIs in Maharashtra, four FHEIs (University of York, University of Bristol, University of Aberdeen and Illinois Institute of Technology) have been given Letter of Approval to start academic operations in Mumbai. University of Southampton and University of New South Wales have already established their campuses in Gurugram and Bengaluru respectively. IIT Madras, IIT Delhi and IIM Ahmedabad have established their overseas campuses at Zanzibar in 2023, Abu Dhabi in 2024 and Dubai respectively in 2025. IIM Ahmedabad launched a one-year fulltime MBA programme in Dubai campus in September 2025, along with a General Management programme, for professionals across the Middle-East, Asia and Africa. The programme has 35 students. IIT Madras, opened its campus at Zanzibar in 2023 - 35 students have graduated with M Tech degrees in Data Science and AI and Ocean Structures so far. Over 100 students are in various BS programmes in Data Science and Chemical Process Engineering. IIT Delhi established its offshore campus in Abu Dhabi, UAE in 2024 with nine UG, PG and Doctoral courses. In the academic year 2025-26, the campus had 171 students. Studying abroad is a matter of individual will and choice, which is contingent on a variety of factors, including affordability, access to finance, exposure to foreign societies and aptitude for particular branches of studies. As per information provided by the Bureau of Immigration (BoI), Ministry of Home Affairs, the number of Indians who disclosed their purpose of visit as STUDY/EDUCATION while going abroad from 2021 to 2025 is as below: Year 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 Number of Students 445580 752100 894758 760060 619264 The Government of India, including under National Education Policy 2020 (NEP 2020) has undertaken several initiatives to ensure availability of high-quality education in the higher education, including through infrastructure upgradation of public funded educational institutions, accreditation of new institutions and courses which meet the criteria under National Accreditation Board, promotion of research & innovation and augmenting digital initiatives for accessibility. These initiatives have contributed to a wider pool of institutions and also in increasing the quality of educational facilities in the country. In addition, University Grants Commission (UGC) has taken several initiatives to enhance quality of education, including financial support to HEIs, including issuing regulations for Joint/Dual/Twinning degree programmes, guidelines for Internship/Apprenticeship Embedded Degree Program, establishment of Research and Development Cells in HEIs, promoting the concept of Professor of Practice, accessibility guidelines and standards for Higher Educational Institutions and Universities, initiation of UTSAH Portal (Undertaking Transformative Strategies and Actions in Higher Education) to track achievements of NEP 2020, issuing Curriculum and Guidelines on Life Skills (Jeevan Kaushal) 2.0, launching of Malaviya Mission Teachers Training Programme (MMTTP) for continuous capacity building of faculties. As an overall result, 52 Indian Institutions are now in the QS World University Ranking (QS WUR) 2027 which is India’s highest ever representation, marking an increase from 11 Indian institutions in QS WUR 2015 . India is ranked 38 th position globally as per Global Innovation Index (2025). India is considered to be one of the largest startup ecosystems in the world (top 3) in scale, funding and unicorn count. Further, to attract international students to India, the Ministry has launched the ‘Study in India’ scheme in 2018 with the aim of promoting India as a global study destination providing world-class education at affordable costs. An integral part of the programme is the Study in India (SII) portal, a one-stop destination for admission and visa applications for all incoming foreign students and acts as a gateway to the Indian higher education ecosystem. There are 1,289 universities, 48,246 colleges and 15,221 stand-alone institutions in the country, of which 87 universities, 5,380 colleges and 2,426 stand-alone institutions are located in Maharashtra. Maharashtra is among the top seven states in the country in terms of student enrolment in higher education, with approximately 46.53 lakh students. Higher education ecosystem in Maharashtra has been significantly strengthened through digital integration, quality accreditation, online learning, institutional governance and financial support through initiatives such as Academic Bank of Credits (ABC), Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR), Study Webs of Active Learning for Young Aspiring Minds (SWAYAM), SAMARTH and PM Vidyalaxmi. The Government has launched the third phase of Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA) in June 2023 in the form of Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM-USHA) for the period 2023-24 to 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs 12,926.10 crore, including the committed liabilities of the earlier phases of RUSA, to cater to the needs of educationally unserved/underserved areas. In Maharashtra, under the Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA), a total of 144 projects, with an approved amount of Rs. 1,431.31 crore (central share: Rs. 863.37 crore), have been approved under various components of the Scheme. title: Parliament Question: Draft UGC Regulations, 2025
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Draft UGC Regulations, 2025 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:34PM by PIB Delhi Education is a subject in the Concurrent List and both the Parliament and the state legislatures have powers to legislate. As per Entry 66 List I of Schedule VII to the Constitution of India, the power to legislate for "Co-ordination and determination of standards in institutions for higher education or research and scientific and technical  institutions", vests in the Central Government. Section 26 (1) (e) of University Grants  Commission (UGC) Act, 1956 empowers UGC to make Regulations regarding ‘defining the qualifications that should ordinarily be required of any person to be appointed to the teaching staff of the University, having regard to the branch of education in which he is expected to give instruction'. Section 26 (1) (g) of UGC Act, 1956 empowers UGC to make regulations 'regulating the maintenance of standards and the co-ordination of work or facilities in Universities’. The Draft UGC Regulations on Minimum Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and Other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges, 2025 were placed on the UGC website on 6 January 2025. In addition, UGC sought feedback from the Principal Secretaries, Higher Education Departments of all States; Higher Education Councils of all States; Offices of the Chancellors of all State Universities; IITs, IIMs, IISERs,  IISc; and other regulatory bodies. The UGC has decided to continue consultations to obtain broader stakeholder inputs before finalizing the Regulations. This approach is intended to ensure that all diverse views expressed on the proposed provisions, including those relating to the appointment of Vice-Chancellors, are duly considered as an integral part of the process of finalizing the Regulations. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298506) आगंतुक पटल  : 40 Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Draft UGC Regulations, 2025 प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:53PM by PIB Delhi Education being a subject of the Concurrent List of the Constitution, both the Centre and States/ UTs are responsible for the Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) and Schools in the country. The Central Higher Education Institutions (CHEIs) under the Ministry of Education including Central Universities, are statutory autonomous organizations established under respective Central Acts of Parliament and governed by provisions of the  Acts/Statutes/Ordinances/Regulations made thereunder. As autonomous institutions, faculty recruitment is done within the institutions itself, in accordance with their Acts and Regulations. The recruitment powers vests with the respective Board of Governors/Executive  Committee/Board of Management. State Universities are established through respective State Acts and vacancies therein are filled by concerned State Governments/ Universities themselves. Vacancy details of State Universities are not maintained centrally. An Institution is declared as Deemed to be University by the Central Government, on the advice of University Grants Commission (UGC), under Section 3 of the UGC Act, 1956. The  Institutions Deemed to be Universities are regulated by the UGC as per the UGC (Institutions  deemed to be Universities) Regulations, 2023. As per these Regulations, the Executive Council of the Institution appoints faculty staff and such other posts on the recommendation of the Selection Committee, in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Minimum  Qualifications for Appointment of Teachers and other Academic Staff in Universities and Colleges and other Measures for the Maintenance of Standards in Higher Education)  Regulations, 2018. Occurring of vacancies and filling thereof is a continuous process. The vacancies arise due to  promotion, retirement, resignation, death, opening of new institutions, schemes or projects, and additional requirements on account of enhanced students’ strength and expansion of capacity  in existing institutions. In centrally financed Higher Education Institutions, measures have been taken to attract quality faculties which includes year-round open advertisements, recruitment through search-cum selection procedures, special recruitment drive, mission mode recruitment and invitation to  alumni/scientists/faculty, etc. The faculty recruitment processes are carried out by the CHEIs by inviting applications in a transparent manner, as part of a multi-step and robust screening process. The Acts and Statutes of various institutions specify the composition of selection  committees, authorities responsible for recruitment of various levels of faculty, provision of  independent subject experts and visitor’s nominees etc. so as to ensure transparency and academic rigour in recruitments. UGC has launched a common portal ‘CU-CHAYAN’ for  faculty recruitment, making provision for listing of vacancies/ advertisements/ jobs across all Central Universities, thus making the entire recruitment process more transparent and accessible. The National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, lays emphasis on improving the overall quality of education in Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) through a set of initiatives that include promotion of multidisciplinary education, nurturing critical thinking and analytical ability, promoting research and innovation, improving the quality of infrastructure, effective and qualitative teacher training etc. To improve the quality of education, several initiatives have been institutionalised in centrally funded institutions. The Government of India provides financial support to state governments under Rashtriya Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (RUSA)/ Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Abhiyan (PM USHA) scheme, for improvement in Higher Education. The Government of India has also launched the Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Program (MMTTP) in 2023 across the country to improve teaching quality, strengthen institutional performance, and promote better academic outcomes in Higher Educational Institutions. The program is implemented through 151 Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Centres (MMTTCs). So far, more than 4 lakh faculty members have been trained across the country. In August, 2021, all CHEIs under the Ministry of Education were requested to undertake a special drive to fill backlog vacancies in their institutions in Mission Mode. The CHEIs undertook  special recruitment drives to fill the vacancies including Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled  Tribes (STs) and Other Backward Classes (OBCs). In September 2022, the Ministry of Education had also exhorted all the CHEIs to fill up the vacancies in Mission Mode. In October 2025, all the CHEIs have again been requested to fill up all the backlog vacancies in Mission Mode.  From September 2022, all CHEIs including Central Universities (CUs) have undertaken Mission Mode recruitment drives to fill the vacancies. Up to 23.05.2026 (i.e. the date of the last  Rozgar Mela), a total number of 32,114 posts have been filled up by all CHEIs, including 18,757  faculty positions, in Mission Mode. This information was given by the Minister of State for Education, Dr Sukanta Majumdar in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** RRTN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298342) आगंतुक पटल  : 94 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Telugu Ministry of Education Parliament Question: Vacancies in Universities प्रविष्टि तिथि:
