title: Government Provides ₹10.66 Crore Financial Assistance to 457 Beneficiaries under Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Inter-Caste Marriages
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Provides ₹10.66 Crore Financial Assistance to 457 Beneficiaries under Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Inter-Caste Marriages प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 2:48PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government has informed the Rajya Sabha that the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages and the Dr. Ambedkar National Relief to the Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes Victims of Atrocities Scheme were merged with the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 , with effect from 31 March 2023 , to avoid duplication in the implementation of schemes. This information was provided by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale , in a written reply to Shri Raghav Chadha in the Rajya Sabha today. The Minister submitted that under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for the Implementation of the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955 and the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 , Central assistance is provided to State Governments and Union Territory Administrations adding that the scheme is implemented by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations, and the responsibility for its effective implementation rests with them. The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation continued to process and provide financial assistance in pending cases pertaining to the Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Social Integration through Inter-Caste Marriages that arose prior to the merger. Accordingly, financial assistance amounting to ₹ 10.66 crore has been released to 457 beneficiaries . The year-wise details show that 68 beneficiaries received financial assistance during 2023-24, 11 beneficiaries during 2024-25 and 378 beneficiaries during 2025-26 , taking the total number of beneficiaries to 457 during the three-year period. ***** PR-67-TAR-KV-GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298179) आगंतुक पटल  : 147 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati , Kannada Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Provides ₹10.66 Crore Financial Assistance to 457 Beneficiaries under Dr. Ambedkar Scheme for Inter-Caste Marriages प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Compounded annual growth rate of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices (2022-23 base) as per revised series during 2022-23 to 2025-26 is 10.88%
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Compounded annual growth rate of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices (2022-23 base) as per revised series during 2022-23 to 2025-26 is 10.88% प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 3:44PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has revised the base year of the National Accounts Statistics from 2011–12 to 2022–23, and the revised series was released in February 2026. As per the revised series (2022–23 base), the contribution of the Manufacturing sector to India's Gross Value Added (GVA) at current prices and the growth rate of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices during the period 2022–23 to 2025–26 are given below: Indicator 2022-23 2023-24 2024-25 (FRE) 2025-26 (PE) Share of Manufacturing in total GVA (in %) 14.7 14.7 14.5 14.8 Change over previous year (in %) - (+)12.7 (+)9.3 (+)10.7 Note: FRE-First Revised Estimates, PE- Provisional Estimates Source: Press Release of Provisional Estimates of GDP dated 05.06.2026 The compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices (2022-23 base) as per the revised series during 2022-23 to 2025-26 is 10.88%. The available data under the respective series do not indicate any significant change in the share of manufacturing in total Gross Value Added (GVA). The Government has undertaken several structural reforms and initiatives to strengthen the resilience of the manufacturing sector and reduce its vulnerability to external shocks. These include, inter-alia, the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Schemes, PM GatiShakti National Master Plan, the National Logistics Policy, Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana (BHAVYA), initiatives to promote semiconductor and electronics manufacturing, critical minerals and Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), and the Scheme for Promotion of Surface Coal/Lignite Gasification Projects, improvement of the ease of doing business, National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP). Collectively, these initiatives seek to strengthen domestic manufacturing, diversify supply chains, reduce import dependence in strategic sectors, enhance energy security and improve the resilience and competitiveness of India's manufacturing ecosystem. This information was given by the Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, Minister of State (Independent Charge) of the Ministry of Planning and Minister of State in the Ministry of Culture Rao Inderjit Singh in the Lok Sabha today. *** Samrat/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298236) आगंतुक पटल  : 234 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation Compounded annual growth rate of Manufacturing GVA at constant prices (2022-23 base) as per revised series during 2022-23 to 2025-26 is 10.88% प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Ministry of Textiles to Celebrate Women Weavers Through ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles Ministry of Textiles to Celebrate Women Weavers Through ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’ Over 100 Women Weavers from Six Handloom Clusters to share their stories of Resilience, Creativity and Role in preserving India’s Weaving Traditions प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:08PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, will organise ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’, a special gathering celebrating the women behind India’s handlooms and recognising their inspiring journeys, voices and contributions to the weaving heritage of the country. The programme will be held on 13 August 2026, at India Habitat Centre, New Delhi. The event will bring together 100+ women weavers from six handloom clusters across India, providing a platform to celebrate their lived experiences, resilience, creativity and role in carrying forward India’s rich weaving traditions. The programme will also witness the release of an anthology featuring the inspiring stories, journeys and voices of these women weavers, bringing their experiences from the loom to a wider audience and highlighting the human stories that lie at the heart of India’s handloom sector. The event will be graced by Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Textiles and Dr. M. Beena, Development Commissioner (Handlooms). Ms. Kanta Singh, Deputy Country Representative, UN Women India, will be the Guest of Honour. ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’ seeks to place women weavers at the centre of the conversation on India’s handloom heritage, acknowledging not only their contribution to the sector but also their individual journeys, aspirations and voices. ****** MAM/VN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298476) आगंतुक पटल  : 94 Ministry of Textiles Ministry of Textiles to Celebrate Women Weavers Through ‘Srijan: Voices from the Loom’ Over 100 Women Weavers from Six Handloom Clusters to share their stories of Resilience, Creativity and Role in preserving India’s Weaving Traditions प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister of Textiles inaugurates IIHT SUTRA 2026, the first National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Textiles Union Minister of Textiles inaugurates IIHT SUTRA 2026, the first National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology Three landmark MoUs signed to strengthen industry, research and academic partnerships for transforming handloom education प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:05PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, today organised IIHT SUTRA 2026 – The Inaugural National Conclave of the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology at Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. Conceived as a first-of-its-kind national platform, IIHT SUTRA 2026 brought together policymakers, academia, industry leaders, research institutions, distinguished alumni and students to deliberate on the future of handloom education and its role in strengthening India's handloom ecosystem. Organised under the theme "IIHTs: Weaving the Future of the Indian Handloom Sector – Educate. Innovate. Transform." , the conclave marked a significant step towards repositioning the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology (IIHTs) as centres of excellence for technical education, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and industry collaboration. The conclave was inaugurated by Shri Giriraj Singh, Union Minister of Textiles , in the presence of Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Textiles , Dr. Beena M., Development Commissioner (Handlooms) and other distinguished dignitaries representing Government, industry, academia and the handloom sector. Addressing the gathering, Union Minister for Textiles Shri. Giriraj Singh , emphasised that India's handloom sector is one of the finest expressions of the country's cultural heritage while also serving as an important source of livelihoods, women's empowerment, exports and sustainable economic development. He observed that preserving India's handloom traditions must go hand in hand with technological advancement, innovation, entrepreneurship and research. He underscored the important role of the IIHTs in developing skilled technocrats capable of supporting productivity enhancement, design innovation, technology upgradation and the long-term competitiveness of the handloom sector. The Minister highlighted that the six Central IIHTs and five State IIHTs have, over the past seven decades, produced generations of skilled professionals who today contribute significantly to industry, entrepreneurship, exports, research and public institutions. He also noted the recent expansion of B.Tech programmes, strengthening of research initiatives, modernisation of laboratories and infrastructure, student support measures and international training programmes undertaken by the IIHTs. In her address, Smt. Neelam Shami Rao, Secretary, Ministry of Textiles , emphasised the need to continuously modernise handloom education by aligning curricula with emerging technologies, strengthening industry partnerships, promoting applied research and encouraging innovation-led learning. She observed that IIHTs must evolve as institutions capable of preparing graduates not only for employment but also for entrepreneurship, leadership and research in the textile and handloom sectors. Welcoming the participants, Dr. Beena M., IAS, Development Commissioner (Handlooms) described IIHT SUTRA as a long-term institutional initiative of the Ministry of Textiles aimed at creating a collaborative national platform for the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology. She stated that the initiative seeks to strengthen partnerships among Government, industry, academia, research institutions and alumni while enabling IIHTs to emerge as future-ready institutions supporting innovation, sustainability, entrepreneurship and technological advancement in the handloom sector. A major highlight of the inaugural session was the exchange of three strategic Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) designed to strengthen institutional collaboration across complementary domains: Grasim Industries Limited – Industry Partnership for curriculum enrichment, internships, industry exposure, skill development and collaborative initiatives. Northern India Textile Research Association (NITRA) – Research and Technology Partnership for collaborative research, testing, innovation, technical support and capacity building. Indian Institute of Management (IIM), Sambalpur – Academic and Management Partnership for leadership development, entrepreneurship, innovation, faculty development and institutional capacity building. These partnerships are expected to provide a structured framework for closer engagement between IIHTs and leading institutions from industry, research and management education, thereby enhancing the quality and relevance of technical education in the handloom sector. During the programme, meritorious students from the IIHTs were honoured with Gold Medals and Rank Certificates in recognition of their outstanding academic performance. The Ministry also released "Handloom Change Makers" , a publication celebrating the achievements of distinguished IIHT alumni who have made notable contributions across industry, entrepreneurship, exports, research and public service. The Union Minister also launched the Ministry's film on IIHTs titled "Weaving India's Handloom Future" , presenting the journey, achievements and future vision of the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology. The film highlights the contribution of IIHTs in developing skilled professionals and supporting the transformation of India's handloom sector. The conclave also featured an exhibition showcasing student innovations, institutional achievements, live demonstrations, research initiatives and emerging technologies adopted by the IIHTs. Participants had the opportunity to interact with students, faculty members and alumni while experiencing the technological and educational capabilities of the institutes. The post-lunch technical session included a panel discussion on "Strengthening Handloom Education through Industry–Academia Collaboration: Curriculum, Skills and Future Readiness." Eminent representatives from industry, academia, research institutions and distinguished alumni deliberated on curriculum reforms, industry partnerships, applied research, entrepreneurship, emerging technologies, skill development and institutional collaboration required to prepare the next generation of professionals for the evolving textile and handloom sector. IIHT SUTRA 2026 represents a significant step towards strengthening the Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology through strategic partnerships, innovation, research and academic excellence, while preparing future-ready professionals for the evolving needs of the Indian handloom sector. ********** MAM/VN (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298473) आगंतुक पटल  : 103 Ministry of Textiles Union Minister of Textiles inaugurates IIHT SUTRA 2026, the first National Conclave of Indian Institutes of Handloom Technology Three landmark MoUs signed to strengthen industry, research and academic partnerships for transforming handloom education प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Development of Tribal Communities under PMJUGA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs Development of Tribal Communities under PMJUGA प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 12:45PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that hon'ble PM launched Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Unnat Gram Abhiyan (PM-JUGA)/ Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, improve access to health, education, Anganwadi facilities and providing livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. The progress made under the abhiyan is as per Annexure I. The state-wise distribution of blocks, villages and ST population covered under DAJGUA is as per Annexure II. title: “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement”
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs “DBT Tribal Portal and Tribal Scholarship Disbursement” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 12:44PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that currently, the Ministry is already leveraging the benefit of DBT Tribal Portal by accessing the data of beneficiaries submitted by the respective State/UT for monitoring and generating MIS reports for the implementation of pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes. The States/UTs have also been given facilities to upload queries, documents, utilization certificates, statement of expenditure etc. which has reduced processing time and reduced grievances. The details of the number of beneficiaries reported by the States/UTs on the DBT Tribal Portal for the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes during the last three financial years are given at Annexure-I. The Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes are the Centrally Sponsored Schemes and implemented through respective States/UTs. The disbursement of scholarships is carried out by the concerned State/UT through their own portal or NSP portal. The progress made through the Portal are given as under: - End-to-End Digitization: Transition from paper-based processing to scheme-specific digital portals. Common Data Standard: Implementation of standard data format for seamless web-service API based data sharing between States/UT portals/ National Scholarship Portal (NSP) and the DBT Tribal Portal of the Ministry Faster Communication and Online Processing: Online upload of Utilization Certificates (UCs), Statements of Expenditure (SoE), and queries by States, significantly reducing processing time and administrative delays. Public Transparency & Outcome Dashboards: Integration of beneficiary and transaction data with the Performance Dashboard of the Ministry, DBT Mission, Prayas Dashboard, and NITI Aayog for outcome tracking. The data of beneficiaries reported by the State/UTs in the DBT Tribal Portal have been useful for monitoring and generating MIS reports. Integration of National Scholarship Portal with States/UTs scholarship portal enables data validation and automated deduplication checks across schemes and databases. Under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Schemes for ST students, to eliminate parking of funds at State level, minimize delays in release of scholarship, and ensure transparency of fund flow, the Ministry has adopted the SNA SPARSH Model for release of central share under Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme. This serves as a Just-in-Time Disbursement Framework under which the Central Share funds are release in "Just-in-time" as and when the bills are raised by respective State Govt for payment of scholarship. Once the bills for scholarship payment is approved, both Central Share as well as State Share fund is directly transferred from RBI account to Student beneficiary account on through DBT. This eliminates the parking of central share funds at state level and minimize delay in disbursement of scholarship. Under Central Sector Schemes of Scholarship implemented directly by the Ministry, a robust digital mechanism is established through the National Scholarship Portal (NSP), Ministry’s Scholarship Portal and the Public Financial Management System (PFMS) to facilitate Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). Removal of physical application process and manual verification by Institute/District/State authorities has streamlined approval workflows and reduced the overall application processing time. Transfer of Scholarship amount through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) into the beneficiary student bank accounts ensures that financial benefit reaches targeted ST students in time and without involvement of intermediaries. The details of the major schemes being implemented by M/o Tribal Affairs are as under: i. Pre-Matric Scholarships to ST students : The scheme is applicable to students who are studying in Classes IX –X. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Scholarship of Rs.225/-per month for day scholars and Rs.525/-per month for hostellers is given for a period of 10 months in a year. Scholarship is disbursed through the State Government/UT Administration. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except North East and Hills States/UT like Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10.For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. ii. Post Matric Scholarship to ST students: The objective of the scheme is to provide financial assistance to the Scheduled Tribe students studying at post-matriculation or post-secondary levels to enable them to complete their education. Parental income from all sources should not be more than Rs.2.50 lakhs per annum. Compulsory fees charged by educational institutions are reimbursed subject to the limit fixed by the concerned State Fee fixation committee and scholarship amount of Rs.230 to Rs.1200 per month, depending upon the course of study is paid. The Scheme is implemented by the State Governments and Union Territory Administrations. Funding ratio is 75:25 between Centre and States for all States except NE and Hilly States/UT of Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Jammu and Kashmir where it is 90:10. For UTs without legislature sharing pattern is 100% Central share. National Fellowship and Scholarship for Higher Education for ST students: This a Central Sector Schemes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. The scheme has two sub-Schemes, viz: iii. a National Scholarship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students (earlier known as Top Class Scholarship Scheme): Under this Scheme, Scholarship is provided for pursuing Graduate/Post Graduate courses in the selected top-class Government and Non-Government Institutes in professional fields such as Management, Medicine, Engineering, Information Technology, Law etc. All the ST students, with annual parental income is not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs and studying in the 265 notified institutes by the Ministry, are eligible to receive scholarship. This scheme is started from year 2007 - 08. b. National Fellowship Scheme for Higher Education of ST Students: It is a Central Sector Scheme, fully funded by Ministry of Tribal Affairs to grant scholarship to meritorious ST students for pursuing Ph.D in India after completion of Master degree. This scheme is started from year 2005-06. The total number of fresh fellowships for Ph.D every year will be 750. ST students with a minimum of 55% marks in Master Degree up to the age of 36 years are eligible to apply for fellowship under the Scheme. The value of fellowship is at par with UGC rates. iv. National Overseas Scholarship for ST students : It is a Central Sector Scheme of Ministry of Tribal Affairs under which scholarships are given to the meritorious Schedule Tribe (ST) students for pursuing higher education in top 1000 ranked (as per latest QS world ranking) Institutes/Universities abroad. This scheme is started from year 1954-55. The Scheme is implemented through the Indian Embassies/Missions abroad, Ministry of External Affairs. Twenty awards are given every year. ST students with annual family income not exceeding Rs.6.0 lakhs are eligible to apply for the Scholarship under the Scheme. v. Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan: Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan Hon'ble PM launched Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan (DAJGUA) on 2nd October, 2024. The Abhiyan comprises of 25 interventions implemented by 17-line Ministries and aims to saturate infrastructural gaps in 63,843 villages, provide social infrastructure like hostels, Anganwadi facilities and mobile medical units and set up Van Dhan Vikas Kendras to provide livelihood opportunities benefiting more than 5 crore tribals in 549 districts and 2,911 blocks in 30 States/UTs in 5 years. The Abhiyan has a total budgetary outlay of Rs.79,156 Cr (Central share: ₹56,333 Cr and State share: ₹22,823 Cr). vi. Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN): Government launched Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM JANMAN) for socio-economic development of 75 PVTG communities residing in 18 states and one UT. The mission aims to provide basic facilities such as safe housing, clean drinking water and improved access to education, health and nutrition, road and telecom connectivity, electrification of unelectrified households and sustainable livelihood opportunities in 3 years. These objectives are planned to be met through 11 interventions including Hostels and Mobile Medical Units (MMUs) implemented by 9-line Ministries. PM JANMAN has total budgetary outlay of Rs.24,104 Cr (Central share: ₹15336 Cr and State share: ₹8768 Cr). vii. Grants under Article 275(1) of the Constitution : Under the Proviso to Article 275(1) of Constitution, Grants are released to States, having ST population for raising the level of administration in Scheduled Areas and for the welfare of tribal people. This is a Special Area Programme and 100% grants are provided to States. Funds are released to the State Governments depending on the felt needs of ST population to bridge the gap in infrastructure activities in the fields of education, health, skill development, livelihood, drinking water, sanitation, etc. viii. Grant-in Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes: Under the scheme of Grant-in-Aid to Voluntary Organizations working for the welfare of Scheduled Tribes, the Ministry funds projects in the fields of education and health, covering residential schools, non-residential schools, hostels, mobile dispensaries, ten or more bedded hospitals, livelihood, etc. ix. Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS): The Scheme provides quality residential education to Scheduled Tribe students in remote and tribal areas with the objective of enabling them to access quality education comparable to the best institutions in the country. The schools provide modern educational infrastructure along with facilities for holistic development of tribal students. Ministry of Tribal Affairs is implementing the Central Sector Scheme of EMRS for providing quality education to tribal students, both boys and girls, in their own environment; the EMRSs are to be at par with Navodaya Vidyalayas, with special facilities for preserving local art and culture besides providing training in sports and skill development. x. Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission (PMJVM): The Mission promotes sustainable livelihoods of Scheduled Tribes through value addition, entrepreneurship development, marketing support and strengthening of tribal producer organisations, with emphasis on value chains based on Minor Forest Produce and other tribal products. xi. Van Dhan Vikas Kendra (VDVK): Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are set up under the Minimum Support Price for Minor Forest Produce scheme, implemented through TRIFED, for value addition and livelihood support to Minor Forest Produce gatherers. xii. Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports Tribal Research Institutes for research, documentation, capacity building, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, awareness generation, information dissemination and evidence-based policy support. xiii. Monitoring, Evaluation, Survey and Social Audit (MESSA): The Scheme supports monitoring, evaluation, impact assessment, surveys and social audit of programmes implemented by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to strengthen evidence-based planning, policy formulation and effective implementation of tribal development initiatives. xiv. Venture Capital Fund for Scheduled Tribes (VCF-ST): The Scheme is implemented through the National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) to provide concessional venture capital assistance to Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs for establishment and expansion of income-generating enterprises. xv. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC): under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs is an apex organisation set up exclusively for economic development of Scheduled Tribes implements various schemes for livelihood generation. NSTFDC extends concessional loans to the eligible Scheduled Tribe communities. These measures help to improve access to education, healthcare, livelihoods and connectivity for tribal communities in Tamil Nadu. These include PMS , PMS , NFHEST , NOS , EMRS and hostels for ST boys and girls to promote education. Healthcare services are strengthened through MMUs and Ayush Wellness Centres in PVTG habitations under PM-JANMAN , and through health and nutrition camps organised under DAJGUA . Livelihood support is provided through VDVKs , PMJVM , term loans, micro-credit and skill development through NSTFDC , DAPST , and convergence with MGNREGA , PM Vishwakarma and PM-KISAN under DAJGUA . Connectivity in tribal areas is being improved through provision of all-weather roads, electrification and telecom connectivity under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA in convergence with the Ministry of Rural Development, State Governments and other implementing agencies. (c): The physical and financial progress of tribal development schemes, including those in Tamil Nadu, is monitored on a continuous basis through the STCMIS portal for Ministry schemes, the PM-JANMAN Dashboard on the PM Gati Shakti portal for real-time habitation-wise monitoring in convergence with the concerned Ministries, regular review meetings with State Governments/UT Administrations on PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA, and periodic assessment of socio-economic indicators of Scheduled Tribes through the Population Census, NFHS and third-party evaluation studies commissioned by the Ministry to assess outcomes and improve programme implementation. These measures help to improve access to education, healthcare, livelihoods and connectivity for tribal communities in Tamil Nadu. These include PMS , PMS , NFHEST , NOS , EMRS and hostels for ST boys and girls to promote education. Healthcare services are strengthened through MMUs and Ayush Wellness Centres in PVTG habitations under PM-JANMAN , and through health and nutrition camps organised under DAJGUA . Livelihood support is provided through VDVKs , PMJVM , term loans, micro-credit and skill development through NSTFDC , DAPST , and convergence with MGNREGA , PM Vishwakarma and PM-KISAN under DAJGUA . Connectivity in tribal areas is being improved through provision of all-weather roads, electrification and telecom connectivity under PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA in convergence with the Ministry of Rural Development, State Governments and other implementing agencies. (c): The physical and financial progress of tribal development schemes, including those in Tamil Nadu, is monitored on a continuous basis through the STCMIS portal for Ministry schemes, the PM-JANMAN Dashboard on the PM Gati Shakti portal for real-time habitation-wise monitoring in convergence with the concerned Ministries, regular review meetings with State Governments/UT Administrations on PM-JANMAN and DAJGUA, and periodic assessment of socio-economic indicators of Scheduled Tribes through the Population Census, NFHS and third-party evaluation studies commissioned by the Ministry to assess outcomes and improve programme implementation. The initiatives in this regard include: (i) Tribal Research, Information, Education, Communication and Events (TRI-ECE): The Scheme supports the Tribal Research Institute of Tamil Nadu for research, documentation, preservation and promotion of tribal art, culture and traditional knowledge systems, along with awareness generation and evidence-based policy support. (ii) Janjatiya Gaurav Divas and Adi Mahotsav: The Ministry observes Janjatiya Gaurav Divas on 15th November every year and organises Adi Mahotsav and similar events to showcase and promote tribal art, culture, cuisine and handicrafts, including those of Tamil Nadu's tribal communities. (iii) Van Dhan Vikas Kendras: VDVKs support Minor Forest Produce-based livelihoods that are intrinsically linked to the traditional occupations and ecological knowledge of tribal communities, thereby supporting continuation of traditional livelihood practices alongside income generation. (iv) EMRS : The preservation and promotion of tribal culture, language and traditional knowledge are integral components of the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) Scheme. To achieve this, Tribal Corners have been established in EMRSs to showcase and preserve the culture, traditions, art, crafts and heritage of tribal communities. Cultural Programs, Meets and workshops are organized to provide a platform for students to learn about, appreciate and celebrate the diverse tribal cultures and traditions of the country. Further, Regional Language Teachers have been recruited in EMRSs enabling students to learn and preserve their regional languages. ***** RN/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298080)

title: Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Tribal Affairs Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Tribal Affairs Shri Durgadas Uikey informed Rajya Sabha that to preserve, document and promote tribal heritage, including tribal art forms, languages, oral traditions and indigenous knowledge systems, the Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides financial assistance to 29 Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs), including the Tribal Research Institute, Jharkhand, under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme "Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)". TRIs function under the administrative control of the respective State Governments/UT Administrations and implement approved Annual Action Plans with financial support from the Ministry. The TRI, Jharkhand undertakes activities such as documentation of tribal languages, folklore, customs and traditional knowledge, organisation of cultural programmes, strengthening of tribal museums and publication of research. The Ministry has also developed digital initiatives for documentation and showcasing tribal cultural resources from Jharkhand through TribeX (erstwhile Adi Sanskriti) digital platform for the preservation and promotion of tribal heritage. Under the Ministry's TribeX initiative, the tribal art forms of Jharkhand, namely Sohrai Painting, Dokra Craft, and Jadupetia Chitrakar, have been included as short-term certificate courses. Further, the Ministry also developed AI based translation tool “Adi Vaani” which supports the preservation and wider accessibility of Jharkhand's tribal languages, including Santhali and Mundari, through AI-enabled text and speech translation between tribal languages and Hindi/English. The implementation of constitutional safeguards and statutory provisions relating to Scheduled Areas, including the provisions of the Fifth Schedule to the Constitution, the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, is primarily the responsibility of the State Government. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs provides policy guidance, advisories and capacity-building support, while Tribal Research Institutes undertake research, studies and documentation to support evidence-based policy formulation and effective implementation. Financial assistance is provided by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs to Tribal Research Institutes under the scheme "Support to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)" for approved activities relating to research, documentation, preservation and promotion of tribal culture, establishment and strengthening of tribal museums, training, publications and dissemination of tribal knowledge. Funds are released to the State Government/Tribal Research Institute based on approved Annual Action Plans, availability of funds and fulfilment of prescribed conditions. Assistance is not released as a separate component exclusively for tribal cultural preservation. Details of the projects/activities sanctioned to Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) are available on the Ministry’s portal: https://tribal.nic.in/Display_Apex_Minutes.aspx As on date, no such proposal is under consideration of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. ***** RN/ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298077) आगंतुक पटल  : 113 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Bengali Ministry of Tribal Affairs Cultural identity, language and traditional rights of Scheduled Tribes प्रविष्टि तिथि:

Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in 2024 for setting up creches प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:07PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (Palna) scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education etc. Anganwadi centres are the world's largest childcare institutions dedicated for providing essential care and support to children ensuring delivery of care facilities till the last mile. Palna is a centrally sponsored scheme and implemented with a funding ratio of 60:40 between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding will be provided by the Central Government. The requirement of Anganwadi-cum-Crèche Centres (AWCCs) is assessed by the respective States/UTs, and proposals are approved by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after detailed discussions with the concerned States/UTs. Presently, a total of 4,172 Anganwadi-cum-Crèches (AWCCs) are operational across the country. Ministry of Women and Child Development has issued National Minimum Standards and Protocol in the year 2024 for setting up creches by care service provider who are required to comply with government rules, laws and regulations related to child protection and safety. Ministry of Labour and Employment has informed that the provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which came into effect on 21.11.2025. Section 67 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for creche facilities for establishment with 50 or more employees. Under the Code, enforcement in respect of establishments under the State Sphere is the responsibility of the respective State Governments. Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Organisation under the Ministry of Labour and Employment is the designated enforcement authority for ensuring compliance with maternity benefit provisions in establishments under the Central Sphere. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children, which are placed under three verticals, viz. (1) Mission Shakti, for safety, protection and empowerment of women; (2) Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0 for improving nutrition & health indicators in the country; and (3) Mission Vatsalya, for protection and welfare of children in difficult circumstances. The ‘Mission Shakti’ aims at strengthening interventions for women safety, security and empowerment. Mission Shakti comprises of two verticals ‘Sambal’ for safety and security of women and ‘Samarthya’ for empowerment of women. The ‘Sambal’ has components of One Stop Centre (OSC), Women Helpline (WHL), Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP) and Nari Adalat. One Stop Centre (OSC) provides integrated and immediate support and assistance under one roof to women affected by violence and those in distress, both in private and public spaces all across the country. It provides services like medical aid, legal aid and advice, temporary shelter, police assistance and psycho-social counselling to needy women across the country. As on date, 991 One Stop Centres have been made operational across the country and since inception, i.e. 1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026, over 15.20 lakh women have been assisted through One Stop Centres across the country. As on date, out of the 39 approved OSCs, 37 OSCs are operational in the State of Odisha, which have assisted over 48,416 women. From 01.07.2020 to FY 2024-25, a total number of 31,547 women has been assisted by OSCs in the State of Odisha. Women Helpline (WHL-181) provides 24-hour toll-free telecommunication services to support women in both emergency and non-emergency situations. It offers assistance to women affected by violence and provides information about government schemes and services. Since inception (1st April, 2015 to 30th June, 2026), over 1.04 crore women have been assisted through Women Helplines across the country. In the State of Odisha, WHL has assisted over 87,675 women till 30th June, 2026. From FY 2020-21 to FY 2024-25, a total number of 33,317 women has been assisted by WHL in the State of Odisha. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao focuses on addressing issues relating to Child Sex Ratio (CSR) and related issues of empowerment of girls and women. The scheme tries to create mindset and behavioural changes towards the girl child by informing, influencing, motivating, engaging and empowering various stakeholders. BBBP has transformed from a policy initiative into a national movement by mobilizing various stakeholders, including government agencies, media, civil society and the public at large. The ‘Samarthya’ has components of Shakti Sadan, Sakhi Niwas, Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY), Palna and SANKALP: Hub for Empowerment of Women (SANKALP: HEW). Shakti Sadan: Under the overarching ‘Mission Shakti’, erstwhile schemes of ‘Swadhar Greh’ – Home for women in difficult circumstances and ‘Ujjawala’- Home for women rescued from Trafficking, have been merged w.e.f. 01.04.2022 and are now known as ‘Shakti Sadan Scheme’, which is an Integrated Relief and Rehabilitation Home for women in distressful situations including trafficked women. It aims at creating a safe and enabling environment for women in such difficult situations, to enable them to overcome the adverse circumstances. Shakti Sadan is helpful towards support for women in distress, providing shelter and rehabilitation support including those affected of trafficking. Presently, 433 Shakti Sadans are functional across the country including 68 in the State of Odisha and 1,46,164 women have been benefitted across the country since inception till 30.06.2026. Sakhi Niwas: Sakhi Niwas Scheme (Working Women Hostel) under the overarching Mission Shakti, aims to promote availability of safe and conveniently located accommodation for working women and for those women who are pursuing higher education and training, with Day care facility for their children in urban, semi-urban and even rural areas where employment opportunity for women exists. Presently, 16 Sakhi Niwas (WWH) is operational in Odisha benefitting around 518 women and 2,32,018 women have been benefitted across the country since inception. Palna: The Ministry introduced Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education etc. As on 31.07.2026, 4172 Anganwadi-cum-creche are operational benefiting about 43,000 beneficiaries across the country. PMMVY: The Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) w.e.f. 01.01.2017 across 35 States and UTs in the country including Odisha (excluding Telangana, which is under process of onboarding on the PMMVY portal). PMMVY is a Centrally Sponsored Maternity Benefit Scheme under which cash incentives of ₹5,000/- is provided directly to the Bank/ Post Office account of the beneficiary in Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) mode for first child. The eligible beneficiaries receive the remaining cash incentive, as per approved norms towards maternity benefit under Janani Suraksha Yojana after institutional delivery, so that on an average a woman gets ₹6,000/-. Cash incentive of ₹6,000/- is also provided under PMMVY to eligible beneficiaries for second child subject to the second child being a girl. The Govt. of Odisha has started the implementation of PMMVY Scheme in their State in FY 2025-26. Benefits amounting to Rs. 21171.32 crores have been extended to more than 4.56 crore women across the country. Further, benefits amounting to Rs. 76.69 crores have been extended to approximately 2.45 lakh women in the State of Odisha through this scheme till 31.07.2026. SANKALP: HEW: The SANKALP: HEW (Hub for Empowerment of Women) functions as a Project Monitoring Unit (PMU) for all components of Mission Shakti. It serves as a single window system to bridge the information and knowledge gap regarding schemes and facilities available for women as well as guide them to avail the benefits and entitlements. As on date, total 35 State SANKALP: HEWs are functional and 742 District SANKALP: HEWs are functional including in the State of Odisha. As on date, 30 District Hubs for Empowerment of Women (DHEWs) are operational in the State of Odisha and 7,75,406 women have been assisted across the country under HEW since the launch of Mission Shakti dashboard. Mission Shakti is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme and implementation of this scheme lies with the State Governments and UT Administrations. Funds are being released on the basis of guidelines of Department of Expenditure, prescribed for Single Nodal agency (SNA) or SNA SPARSH of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Once in a year, the Programme Approval Board (PAB) monitors with States and UTs the progress of activities under the scheme and reviews status of achievement of objectives, effective delivery of services to women and children. The States/UTs assess their requirement as per local needs and proposals are approved every year by the Programme Approval Board (PAB) after discussion with States/UTs. Further, the implementation and coverage of the Schemes under Mission Shakti varies across States/UTs depending upon their population, geographical spread, local requirements and demand for various services and interventions. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Rajya Sabha in reply to a question. **** SS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298273) आगंतुक पटल  : 94 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry of Women and Child Development is implementing Centrally Sponsored Schemes in the country for the welfare of women and children प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Government remains committed to ensuring that children are able to benefit from digital technologies while being protected from online harms
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Government remains committed to ensuring that children are able to benefit from digital technologies while being protected from online harms प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:05PM by PIB Delhi The Government recognizes the transformative potential of emerging digital technologies, particularly in enhancing access to education, information and services for children. At the same time, the Government is cognizant of the associated risks, including exposure to harmful content, cyberbullying, online abuse, excessive screen time and digital dependency, thereby necessitating appropriate safeguards for children in the digital environment. The Government has put in place a comprehensive legal and regulatory framework under the Information Technology Act, 2000, the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 (as amended), and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 to ensure a safe, secure and accountable online environment for users, including children. The Information Technology Act, 2000, read with the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021, provides a comprehensive legal framework to ensure a safe and accountable online environment. The Rules mandate intermediaries to exercise due diligence and prohibit hosting or transmission of unlawful content, including content that is obscene, pornographic, invasive of privacy, harmful to children, promotes hate or violence, impersonates individuals, or threatens public order. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 further provides safeguards for children by requiring verifiable consent of parents or lawful guardians prior to processing of their personal data and prohibits practices such as tracking, behavioural monitoring and targeted advertising directed at children. The DPDP Rules prescribe operational mechanisms for obtaining verifiable parental consent, including through identity and age verification measures and the use of virtual tokens. It also provides for the right to withdraw consent, with corresponding obligations on data fiduciaries to erase such data in accordance with the provisions of the Act. The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has established the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) to provide a framework and eco-system for Law Enforcement Agencies to deal with cyber-crimes in a comprehensive and coordinated Manner. The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (https://cybercrime.gov.in) enables the public to report all types of cybercrimes, with special emphasis on crimes against children. To strengthen a comprehensive and coordinated response mechanism to deal with cybercrimes, the Central Government has implemented measures such as raising public awareness, issuing alerts and advisories, training LEA personnel, prosecutors and judicial officers, and upgrading cyber forensic facilities. The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has developed several resources to promote online safety. These include the “Being Safe Online” guidelines for awareness among children, parents, educators and the public; the Manual on Safety and Security of Children in Schools incorporating guidelines for prevention of cyberbullying; and the Guidelines on Preventing Cyber Bullying for school children issued in 2024. These resources provide information regarding online safety, reporting mechanisms, preventive measures and responsible online behaviour. During 2025-26, NCPCR conducted conferences at State and district levels across the country on child rights issues, including school safety and cyber safety, and organised capacity-building programmes for school administrators and educators on child protection laws and safety practices. NCPCR is also conducting virtual district workshops on school safety and child security. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) commissioned a national level study on “Effects (Physical, Behavioural and Psycho- social) of using mobile phones and other devices with internet accessibility by children” in 2021. The main objective of the study was to understand physical, behavioural, and psycho-social effects on children of using mobile phones and other devices with internet accessibility. This was a nationwide study of all regions. The total number of responses collected were of 5,811 participants, consisting of 3,491 school going children, 1,534 parents and 786 teachers from 60 schools, across six states in the country. The study report is available on NCPCR’s website at- https://ncpcr.gov.in/public/viewPdf/165650458362bc410794e02_effect1.PDF The Ministry of Education issued the PRAGYATA Guidelines on Digital Education in July 2020, which provide a framework for safe and effective online learning, including promotion of students’ well-being and responsible use of social media and electronic devices. CBSE has supplemented these efforts through guidelines on digital etiquette, cybersecurity training for teachers, publication of the Cyber Security Handbook and advisories to schools for establishing Cyber Clubs to promote cyber safety awareness. NCERT has also incorporated cyber safety in its curriculum and developed resource materials on cyber safety and security. The Government remains committed to ensuring that children are able to benefit from digital technologies while being protected from online harms. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. Savitri Thakur in Rajya Sabha in reply to a question. **** SS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2298276) आगंतुक पटल  : 87 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Women and Child Development Government remains committed to ensuring that children are able to benefit from digital technologies while being protected from online harms प्रविष्टि तिथि:

ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
title: Government accords highest priority for ensuring safety and security of children and has undertaken various initiatives in this regard
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Government accords highest priority for ensuring safety and security of children and has undertaken various initiatives in this regard प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:04PM by PIB Delhi Government accords the highest priority for ensuring safety and security of children and has undertaken various initiatives in this regard. To safeguard children against sexual abuse and sexual harassment, Government has enacted The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. It defines a child as any person below the age of 18 years. The Act was amended in 2019 to introduce more stringent punishment including death penalty for committing sexual crimes on children, with a view to deter the perpetrators & prevent such crimes. The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Rules, 2020 provide a child-friendly legal framework for the protection of children from sexual offences. Rule 4 of the POCSO Rules, 2020 provides for the appointment of a Support Person to render assistance to the child throughout the process of investigation and trial, wherever deemed necessary by the Child Welfare Committee. The Support Person is a person or organization working in the field of child rights or protection, recognized by the District Child Protection Unit (DCPU), or a person employed by the DCPU. The Support Person is responsible for facilitating access to support services, keeping the child and family informed about the progress of the case, coordinating with concerned authorities, safeguarding the best interests of the child, and maintaining confidentiality throughout the legal process. Further, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has issued the "Model Guidelines with respect to Support Persons under Section 39 of the POCSO Act, 2012", which, inter alia, provide for the constitution of a Selection Committee for empanelment of Support Persons, prescribe their qualifications, roles and responsibilities, and lay down the procedure for their selection and deployment. The primary objective of the Support Person is to provide emotional and psychological support to child victims during the legal process and to ensure their well-being, protection and access to appropriate services. To facilitate monitoring and coordination among stakeholders, NCPCR has developed the POCSO Tracking Portal for real-time tracking of cases relating to child sexual abuse. The Portal also captures information regarding the appointment of Support Persons in POCSO cases. To safeguard children against sexual abuse and sexual harassment, Government has enacted The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012. The primary objective of the Support Person is to provide emotional and psychological support to child victims during the legal process and to ensure their well-being, protection and access to appropriate services. title: Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches under Palna for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Women and Child Development Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches under Palna for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:03PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry introduced Anganwadi cum Creches (AWCCs) under Palna Scheme w.e.f. 01 April 2022, for providing day care creche facilities in safe and secure environment to children (aged 06 months – 06 years) of all mothers irrespective of their employment status along with nutritional support, health and cognitive development of children, growth monitoring, immunization, education etc. Palna component under Samarthya vertical of Mission Shakti is a centrally sponsored scheme and is implemented with a funding ratio of 60:40 between Centre and State Governments and UTs with legislature except North East & Special Category States where ratio is 90:10. For UTs without legislature, 100% funding is provided by the Central Government. Funds under the Scheme are released to the States/UTs in accordance with the guidelines of the Department of Expenditure through the Single Nodal Agency (SNA)/SNA-SPARSH mechanism of the Public Financial Management System (PFMS). Presently, a total of 4,172 Anganwadi-cum-Crèches (AWCCs) are operational across the country. Ministry of Labour and Employment has informed that the provisions of the Maternity Benefit Act, 1961 have been subsumed under the Code on Social Security, 2020, which came into effect on 21.11.2025. Section 67 of the Code on Social Security, 2020 provides for creche facilities for establishment with 50 or more employees. Under the Code, enforcement in respect of establishments under the State Sphere is the responsibility of the respective State Governments. Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) Organisation under the Ministry of Labour and Employment is the designated enforcement authority for ensuring compliance with maternity benefit provisions in establishments under the Central Sphere. This information was given by the Minister of State for Women and Child Development Smt. title: India’s Infrastructure Transformation: From Connectivity to Capacity
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder India’s Infrastructure Transformation: From Connectivity to Capacity प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:48PM by PIB Delhi Building the Foundation of Growth India’s infrastructure landscape has undergone a major transformation over the past 12 years. From transport and logistics to housing and water, infrastructure development has moved towards integrated planning and large-scale expansion. This has strengthened connectivity, improved access to essential services and created the foundations for sustained economic growth. Public capital expenditure has risen from about ₹2 lakh crore in FY 2014–15 to ₹12.2 lakh crore in FY 2026–27 , supporting this advancement. A New Era of Rail Mobility Indian Railways is moving towards faster, safer and more modern mobility. Electrification, advanced safety systems, high-speed rail and new-generation trains are reshaping the rail network. Railway budget increased from ₹32,000 crore in 2014–15 to ₹2.78 lakh crore in FY2026–27. Rail electrification increased from about 20% before 2014 to 99.6% by July 2026 . 162 Vande Bharat , 2 Vande Bharat Sleeper Services and 72 Amrit Bharat services have improved connectivity and travel experience. The Kavach Version 4.0 has been commissioned on 2,633 route km as of July 2026 . The Mumbai–Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor is being developed over a 508 km route with a design speed of 350 kmph . Of the 1,340 stations identified under the Amrit Bharat Station Scheme , redevelopment has been completed for 261 stations as on 18 July 2026. First indigenously developed Hydrogen Fuel Cell Trainset has been launched in July 2026. It is a 10-coach train with capacity for around 2,600 passengers , running on the Jind–Sonipat section. It generates its own electricity onboard with water vapour and heat as the only by-product. Roads and Highways Connecting India A wider and more capable road network is bringing regions closer. The expansion of National Highways, rural roads and major corridors is enabling smoother movement of people and goods. India has the world’s second-largest road network at 63.73 lakh km . Length of national highways increased by about 61%, from 91,287 km in FY 14 to 1,46,572 km in March 2026 . The length of four-lane and above national highways increased from 18,371 km in 2014 to 45,516 km. The length of roads increased from 3.86 lakh km during 2000–2014 to 4.11 lakh km during 2014–2026 under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana. Since September 2024, PMGSY-IV has been launched with an objective to provide connectivity to 25,000 unconnected habitations by the year 2029. Under Bharatmala, 22,590 km of roads have been completed till 31 March 2026 . Bridges and Tunnels: Engineering New Frontiers Engineering breakthroughs are overcoming some of India’s most demanding geographical challenges. These projects are opening new routes across difficult terrain. Chenab Bridge (2025): World's highest railway arch bridge, standing 359 m above the Chenab River; 1,315 m steel structure strengthening Jammu–Srinagar connectivity. Anji Khad Bridge (2025): India's first cable-stayed railway bridge, in Jammu & Kashmir. Pamban Bridge (2025): India's first vertical-lift railway sea bridge, connecting Rameswaram to the mainland; 2.07 km with a 72.5 m vertical lift span. Z-Morh/Sonamarg Tunnel (2025): 12 km tunnel providing all-weather access through avalanche-prone terrain in J&K, improving movement towards Ladakh. Sudarshan Setu (2024): 2.32 km bridge connecting Okha with Beyt Dwarka, Gujarat. Atal Tunnel (2020): 9.02 km — world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 feet, connecting Manali and Lahaul-Spiti. Dr. Syama Prasad Mukherjee Tunnel (2017): 9 km all-weather tunnel between Jammu and Srinagar, cutting travel time by ~2 hours. Civil Aviation and Regional Air Access Air connectivity is reaching more cities, towns and remote regions. The expansion of airports, UDAN routes and digital passenger services is making flying more accessible across the country. UDAN connected 95 airports, heliports, and water aerodromes through 679 routes , benefiting over 1.68 crore passengers as on 15 July 2026. Operational airports increased from 74 in 2014 to 165 in July 2026 . 25 greenfield airports have been approved after 2014. Digi Yatra is active at 38 airports. The app has enabled over 10 crore seamless journeys with over 2.4 crore downloads . Modified UDAN has been approved in March 2026 for FY 2026–27 to FY 2035–36 with an outlay of ₹28,840 crore , envisioning 100 new airports and 200 modern helipads to strengthen last-mile regional air connectivity. Metro: The Rise of Mass Urban Transit India’s urban mobility network is expanding in scale and scope. Metro connectivity now spans more cities, while innovative systems are opening new possibilities for urban transport. Metro network expanded from 248 km in 2014 to over 1,155 km in 2026 . Cities with metro connectivity increased from 5 to 26 , while daily ridership crossed 1.15 crore passengers . Kolkata operationalised India’s first underwater metro tunnel in 2024. Kochi operationalised India’s first Water Metro system with the first boat launched in December 2021. India’s Maritime Momentum India is strengthening its maritime backbone to support a growing economy and expanding trade. Investments in ports, waterways and maritime infrastructure are creating a more capable and connected ecosystem. Major ports’ cargo handling capacity nearly doubled from 873 MMTPA in 2014 to 1,728 MMTPA in 2026 . Vessel turnaround time improved from 94 hours to 48.8 hours in 2025-26 . Major ports collectively handled 915.17 MT of cargo during FY 2025-26, increasing from 581 MT in FY 2014-15 . The Sagarmala Programme strengthened port-led development, coastal connectivity, and logistics integration. National waterways increased from 5 in 2014 to 111 in 2026 , of which 32 are operational . India became the world's No. 1 ship-recycling nation in 2025 , with its global share rising from 30.1% (2024) to 35.4% (2025) — recycling 2.99 million gross tons (GT) , up nearly 60% from 1.86 million GT in 2024. Jawaharlal Nehru Port ranked 22 nd as per the Container Port Performance Index (CPPI) 2025, published by the World Bank. Bharat Maritime Insurance Pool (BMIP) has been launched on 12 May 2026. It is a USD 1.5 billion domestic insurance pool with a sovereign guarantee of USD 1.4 billion (₹12,980 crore), covering Hull & Machinery, Cargo, Protection and Indemnity, and War risk for Indian-flagged/controlled vessels. As on 29th July 2026, a total of 1608 policies covering Cargo War risks and Hull War risks have been issued under the Pool. Strengthening Logistics and Industrial Capacity Infrastructure is increasingly being planned as an interconnected network supporting industry and trade. From GatiShakti to industrial corridors, the focus is on improving coordination, efficiency and manufacturing capacity. PM GatiShakti National Master Plan integrated infrastructure planning across 58 Ministries and Departments using over 3,291 data layers . As on 11 August 2026, 396 infrastructure projects with a total estimated cost of about ₹18.66 Lakh Crore have been evaluated through the Network Planning Group mechanism. Out of these, 256 projects have been sanctioned and 198 projects are under implementation. The National Logistics Policy has strengthened multimodal logistics efficiency and supply chain integration. PRAGATI reviewed 382 projects worth over ₹85 lakh crore and resolved 2,958 issues . Over 4,220 industrial parks are mapped on the India Industrial Land Bank (IILB) . 272 plug-and-play industrial parks are operational across the country. 20 industrial smart cities have been approved across 7 industrial corridors . The BHAVYA scheme has been approved in March 2026 to develop 100 new plug-and-play industrial parks . BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme has been approved on 24 July 2026, with an outlay of ₹3,030 crore . The scheme will be implemented over five years, from FY2026–27 to FY2030–31. 7 Pradhan Mantri MITRA Parks have been proposed to strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem. Water, Housing and Urban Development The infrastructure push extends directly to people’s homes and everyday needs. From tap-water access and affordable housing to urban renewal, these efforts are shaping better living conditions across rural and urban India. Under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) , rural tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore in 2019 to around 15.91 crore households as on 10 th August 2026. JJM 2.0 has been approved in March 2026. The mission has been extended to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore . Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) , 99.25 lakh houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026. Around 96% of houses under PMAY-U 2.0 are allotted to women. Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Grameen (PMAY-G), out of the 3.91 crore houses sanctioned, 3.13 crore houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026.  Nearly 75% of the houses sanctioned under PMAY-G are either in the name of women or under joint ownership. The SWAMIH Fund launched in 2019 delivered over 63,000 homes , benefiting around 2.52 lakh people as of June 2026. Under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 , projects worth about ₹2.79 lakh crore have been sanctioned since 2015. Under Smart Cities Mission, a total of 7,790 projects worth ₹1,56,257 crore have been completed as of March 2026. Infrastructure for a Stronger, Future-Ready India India’s infrastructure journey reflects a decisive shift in the scale and ambition of national development. The focus has moved towards building resilient, high-capacity systems that not only support a fast-growing economy today but also anticipate the needs of tomorrow. Collectively, these initiatives are strengthening the foundation for a more efficient, inclusive, and future-ready India. Over 4,220 industrial parks are mapped on the India Industrial Land Bank (IILB) . 272 plug-and-play industrial parks are operational across the country. 20 industrial smart cities have been approved across 7 industrial corridors . The BHAVYA scheme has been approved in March 2026 to develop 100 new plug-and-play industrial parks . BHAVYA Rasayan Scheme has been approved on 24 July 2026, with an outlay of ₹3,030 crore . The scheme will be implemented over five years, from FY2026–27 to FY2030–31. 7 Pradhan Mantri MITRA Parks have been proposed to strengthen the manufacturing ecosystem. Water, Housing and Urban Development The infrastructure push extends directly to people’s homes and everyday needs. From tap-water access and affordable housing to urban renewal, these efforts are shaping better living conditions across rural and urban India. Under Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) , rural tap water coverage increased from 3.23 crore in 2019 to around 15.91 crore households as on 10 th August 2026. JJM 2.0 has been approved in March 2026. The mission has been extended to December 2028, with an enhanced outlay of ₹8.69 lakh crore . Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Urban (PMAY-U) , 99.25 lakh houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026. Around 96% of houses under PMAY-U 2.0 are allotted to women. Under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana-Grameen (PMAY-G), out of the 3.91 crore houses sanctioned, 3.13 crore houses have been completed as on 12 August 2026.  Nearly 75% of the houses sanctioned under PMAY-G are either in the name of women or under joint ownership. The SWAMIH Fund launched in 2019 delivered over 63,000 homes , benefiting around 2.52 lakh people as of June 2026. Under AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 , projects worth about ₹2.79 lakh crore have been sanctioned since 2015. Under Smart Cities Mission, a total of 7,790 projects worth ₹1,56,257 crore have been completed as of March 2026. Infrastructure for a Stronger, Future-Ready India India’s infrastructure journey reflects a decisive shift in the scale and ambition of national development. The focus has moved towards building resilient, high-capacity systems that not only support a fast-growing economy today but also anticipate the needs of tomorrow. Collectively, these initiatives are strengthening the foundation for a more efficient, inclusive, and future-ready India.
