title: Empowering Governance through Digital Infrastructure
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Empowering Governance through Digital Infrastructure प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 6:20PM by PIB Delhi Building a Connected and Citizen-Centric India India's governance has undergone a fundamental transformation through Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI). Public services that once depended on extensive paperwork and physical offices are now available through integrated digital platforms. Over the past 12 years, DPI has connected citizens, governments and institutions on an unprecedented scale. It has made governance faster, transparent and more responsive to citizens' needs. Digital infrastructure has also emerged as a cornerstone of India's economic growth. Digital Economy now contributes about 12–14% of India's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and is projected to account for 20% over the next decade. India is now the world’s fifth-largest digitalised economy and the fourth-highest ranked G20 economy, according to the State of India’s Digital Economy Report 2026.  As India marks its 80th Independence Day , the continued expansion of digital governance is strengthening service delivery, enabling economic opportunities and advancing the vision of Viksit Bharat . Key Milestones in India’s Digital Self-Reliance Landscape Electronics Manufacturing: Driving India's Self-Reliance Guided by the vision of Make in India, India has emerged as a global hub for electronics manufacturing. Flagship initiatives, including the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme, Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), India Semiconductor Mission (ISM), Modified Electronics Manufacturing Clusters (EMC 2.0), have strengthened domestic manufacturing in India. 7-Fold Growth in Electronics Production: Electronics production increased from ₹1.9 lakh crore in 2014–15 to ₹13.11 lakh crore in 2025–26. 11-Fold Rise in Electronics Exports: Electronics exports grew from ₹38,000 crore to ₹4.24 lakh crore during the same period. Third-largest Export Sector: Electronic goods have now become India's third-largest export category, with exports reaching USD 47.96 billion in FY 2025-26. Employment and Women Participation: Electronic manufacturing ecosystem supports nearly 25 lakh jobs, with women accounting for nearly 30% of the workforce. Building India's Semiconductor Ecosystem The Union Cabinet approved Semicon 2.0 with an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore to strengthen India's semiconductor ecosystem. Under ISM 1.0, 12 semiconductor units worth ₹1.64 lakh crore have been approved. Three facilities have already started commercial production, with another unit expected to commence operations this year. Mobile Phones: A Major Driver of Growth Global Mobile Manufacturing Hub: India is now the world's 2nd largest mobile phone manufacturer, with mobile phones rising from the 153rd largest export item in FY 2014-15 to become India's largest export product in FY 2025-26. 33-fold increase in mobile phone production: Production rose from ₹18,000 crore in 2014–15 to ₹6.27 lakh crore in 2025–26. 165-fold surge in mobile phone exports: Exports increased from ₹1,500 crore to ₹2.59 lakh crore over the same period. Employment and Women Participation: Out of 12 lakh jobs in mobile manufacturing segment, women constitute nearly 70% of the workforce. Enhanced Telecommunications Infrastructure Telephone Connectivity: Telephone connections increased from 93.3 crore in 2014 to 134.8+ crore at the end of June 2026. Higher Tele-density: Tele-density grew from 75.23% in 2014 to 94.31% at the end of June 2026. Wireless Mobile Subscribers: The number of active wireless mobile subscribers reached 1201.06 million in June 2026. Internet and Digital Connectivity Internet Users Quadrupled: Internet subscribers increased from 25.15 crore in 2014 to 109.2+ crore at the end of March 2026. Affordable Mobile Data: Wireless data cost dropped drastically from ₹ 308/GB in 2014 to ₹7.51/GB in 2026, making digital services more affordable. Mobile broadband speed: Average mobile broadband download speed has increased from 13.67 Mbps in March 2022 to 132.00 Mbps in December 2025 as per Ookla’s global speedtest index. Nationwide 5G Rollout: 5G services are now available in 99.9% of districts across all States and Union Territories. The number of 5G Base Transceiver Stations (BTSs) has now reached 5.63 lakh in June 2026. Expanding Rural Mobile Connectivity: A total of 6.31 lakh villages have been now covered with 4G services by BSNL and other operators. Connectivity under BharatNet Initiative: As of June 2026, 2.21 lakh Gram Panchayats are service-ready, supported by over 8.5 lakh route km of optical fibre cable. PM-WANI: PM-WANI provides affordable public Wi-Fi through a distributed network of public data offices and other ecosystem partners. Over 4 lakh hotspots have been deployed nationwide, as of 28 February 2026. New reforms introduced in May 2026 enable QR-based authentication, 15, 30 and 60-minute Wi-Fi plans, and standardised hotspot names. India is Preparing for the 6G Era The Bharat 6G Vision aims to position India among the global leaders in 6G technology by 2030, with a focus on indigenous research, intellectual property, standards development and next-generation telecom innovation. UPI: Powering Seamless Digital Payments UPI accounts for nearly 50% of global real-time payment transaction volume, making it the world's largest real-time payment system by volume. Volume of Transactions: UPI processed 24,161.69 crore transactions worth ₹314.23 lakh crore in FY 2025–26. India’s Largest Digital Payments Network : UPI serves more than 55.49 crore individuals, 6.5 crore merchants, and connects 731 banks on one platform, making it the world’s largest digital payment system. Share of UPI in India's Digital Payments: UPI accounted for 85% of India's digital payment transactions by volume in FY 2025–26. Monthly Transactions Soar: UPI transactions increased from 0.01 crore in a month in 2016 to 2,000+ crore transactions in a month by 2025, reflecting its rapid adoption across India. UPI Goes Global : UPI is now accepted in 11 foreign countries like Cambodia, Singapore, UAE, France, Mauritius etc. Digital Commerce Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) : ONDC is building an open digital commerce ecosystem connecting buyers and sellers across platforms. By June 2026, it had over 20 crore buyers, 5 lakh sellers, presence in 1,000 cities and nearly 90 lakh monthly transactions. Its integration with eSaras and Indiahandmade has expanded market access for SHGs, weavers and artisans across 11+ buyer apps, while the Sahayak WhatsApp Bot supports small businesses in 5 languages. Government e-Marketplace (GeM): GeM has transformed public procurement by making it transparent, efficient and paperless. By June 2026, it recorded over ₹18.4 lakh crore in cumulative Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), including ₹5 lakh crore in FY 2025–26, and enabled over 11 lakh MSMEs to access government markets. SWAYATT (Startup Runway for Women and Youth-led Enterprises) initiative, promotes inclusive public procurement through the GeM by enabling startups, women and youth-led enterprises to directly access government buyers. By FY 2025–26, women-led businesses recorded ₹ 83,323 crore and startups ₹ 54,005.8 crore in cumulative order value, demonstrating the initiative’s growing reach. E-Governance Initiatives Revolutionising G2C Services DigiLocker: DigiLocker is replacing physical documents with a secure digital wallet. As of 31 July 2026, the platform has registered over 72 crore users and issued more than 934+ Cr documents. UMANG: UMANG has become a single digital gateway for government services, expanding from 166 services in 2017 to 2585 services as of 23 July 2026. Transactions have grown from 4.6 crore to over 798 crore as of 23 July 2026, reflecting widespread digital adoption. Aadhaar: Aadhaar created a trusted biometric identity platform for secure and instant digital authentication. Aadhaar generation increased from 0.42 crore in 2010-11 to over 145 crore by July 2026. Common Service Centres: CSCs provide physical access points for Government-to-Citizen (G2C) e-services, reducing the need to visit government offices. As of June 2026, more than 5.16 lakh CSCs were functional across India. Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT): Aadhaar-linked DBT enables direct transfer of welfare benefits from 318 schemes across 56 Ministries into beneficiaries’ bank accounts. More than ₹52 lakh crore has been transferred through DBT across the country. Read More: The Digital India Digital Platforms Driving Educational Access DIKSHA: DIKSHA provides curriculum-linked content, QR-coded textbooks, teacher training and accessible learning resources. It has 2.35 crore registered users and 3.58 lakh daily active users, as on 10 August 2026. SWAYAM : SWAYAM offers free courses from Class IX to postgraduate level. The platform hosts over 20,000 courses across disciplines with 6.5 crore+ total enrollments, as of 10 August 2026. SWAYAM Prabha: It uses 40 DTH channels to broadcast high-quality educational programmes 24×7 through the GSAT-15 satellite, enabling students to access learning without internet connectivity. PM e-Vidya: PM e-Vidya integrates DIKSHA, SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, community radio and educational television to support uninterrupted and inclusive learning. Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR): APAAR provides students with a unique digital academic identity for storing and verifying academic records. More than 33.74 crore APAAR IDs had been generated by June 2026. A Stronger Framework Against Exam Fraud The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 31 July 2026, proposes tougher penalties and a time-bound justice mechanism. Under the Bill, individual offenders face 5–10 years’ imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh, service providers face fines up to ₹5 crore and an 8-year ban, while organised exam-fraud syndicates face 7–10 years’ imprisonment and a minimum fine of ₹10 crore. Investigations must be completed within 2 months, trials within 3 months of filing the chargesheet, and appeals before the High Court are to be disposed of within 3 months of admission. Powering India’s Digital Workforce FutureSkills PRIME: It equips learners with cutting-edge skills essential in today's rapidly evolving digital landscape. The platform has 34 lakh+ registered users for digital skills, as of 10 August 2026. Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) : SIDH brings skilling, digital learning and employment opportunities onto a single platform. As of 2 August 2026, it has 20.10 million registrations, offers 3,643 self-paced courses, and has generated 1 million+ opportunities. National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT): NIELIT delivers digital literacy and skill development programmes, including Awareness in Computer Concepts (ACC) and Course on Computer Concepts (CCC), through 56 centres and over 9,000 partner institutes across India. More than 31.92 lakh candidates have been trained over the last three financial years. IndiaAI Mission: The IndiaAI Mission is strengthening AI education, infrastructure and responsible AI adoption. It is promoting AI skilling across schools, higher education institutions and professional training programmes through initiatives such as IndiaAI Kosh. Read More: Transforming India with AI India’s Growing Digital Rise India’s digital rise is transforming the way citizens, businesses and institutions interact with the government and economy. A rapidly expanding digital ecosystem is enabling faster services, greater transparency and wider access. Digital Public Infrastructure is creating a strong foundation for innovation, entrepreneurship and inclusive growth. The growing adoption of emerging technologies is opening new opportunities across sectors and strengthening India’s global digital presence. Digital capabilities are also making governance more responsive, efficient and citizen-centric. This transformation is positioning technology as a key enabler of economic opportunity and social development. Together, these advances are strengthening the foundations of a digitally empowered and Viksit Bharat. It has 2.35 crore registered users and 3.58 lakh daily active users, as on 10 August 2026. SWAYAM : SWAYAM offers free courses from Class IX to postgraduate level. The platform hosts over 20,000 courses across disciplines with 6.5 crore+ total enrollments, as of 10 August 2026. SWAYAM Prabha: It uses 40 DTH channels to broadcast high-quality educational programmes 24×7 through the GSAT-15 satellite, enabling students to access learning without internet connectivity. PM e-Vidya: PM e-Vidya integrates DIKSHA, SWAYAM, SWAYAM Prabha, community radio and educational television to support uninterrupted and inclusive learning. Automated Permanent Academic Account Registry (APAAR): APAAR provides students with a unique digital academic identity for storing and verifying academic records. More than 33.74 crore APAAR IDs had been generated by June 2026. A Stronger Framework Against Exam Fraud The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 31 July 2026, proposes tougher penalties and a time-bound justice mechanism. Under the Bill, individual offenders face 5–10 years’ imprisonment and a fine up to ₹50 lakh, service providers face fines up to ₹5 crore and an 8-year ban, while organised exam-fraud syndicates face 7–10 years’ imprisonment and a minimum fine of ₹10 crore. Investigations must be completed within 2 months, trials within 3 months of filing the chargesheet, and appeals before the High Court are to be disposed of within 3 months of admission. Powering India’s Digital Workforce FutureSkills PRIME: It equips learners with cutting-edge skills essential in today's rapidly evolving digital landscape. The platform has 34 lakh+ registered users for digital skills, as of 10 August 2026. Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) : SIDH brings skilling, digital learning and employment opportunities onto a single platform. As of 2 August 2026, it has 20.10 million registrations, offers 3,643 self-paced courses, and has generated 1 million+ opportunities. National Institute of Electronics and Information Technology (NIELIT): NIELIT delivers digital literacy and skill development programmes, including Awareness in Computer Concepts (ACC) and Course on Computer Concepts (CCC), through 56 centres and over 9,000 partner institutes across India. More than 31.92 lakh candidates have been trained over the last three financial years. IndiaAI Mission: The IndiaAI Mission is strengthening AI education, infrastructure and responsible AI adoption. It is promoting AI skilling across schools, higher education institutions and professional training programmes through initiatives such as IndiaAI Kosh. Read More: Transforming India with AI India’s Growing Digital Rise India’s digital rise is transforming the way citizens, businesses and institutions interact with the government and economy. A rapidly expanding digital ecosystem is enabling faster services, greater transparency and wider access. Digital Public Infrastructure is creating a strong foundation for innovation, entrepreneurship and inclusive growth. The growing adoption of emerging technologies is opening new opportunities across sectors and strengthening India’s global digital presence. Digital capabilities are also making governance more responsive, efficient and citizen-centric. This transformation is positioning technology as a key enabler of economic opportunity and social development. Together, these advances are strengthening the foundations of a digitally empowered and Viksit Bharat. title: The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder The New Era of Indian Agriculture and Allied Sectors “Driving Growth, Resilience and Food Security” प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:36PM by PIB Delhi Driving Agricultural Transformation India’s agriculture and allied sectors are witnessing a significant transformation, marked by rising productivity, stronger farmer support systems, and greater resilience. Agriculture remains the backbone of India's economy, providing livelihoods to approximately 46.1 percent of the workforce. Livestock and fisheries have maintained stable growth of 5-6 percent , strengthening rural incomes and supporting agricultural diversification. Over the past decade, sustained policy interventions have improved access to credit, insurance, and markets, and accelerated the adoption of digital technologies. Growing investments in food processing, cooperatives, livestock, dairy, and fisheries are enabling greater value addition, income diversification, and employment across the agricultural value chain. Strengthening the Agricultural Economy The GVA of the Agriculture and Allied Sector increased from Rs. 20.94 lakh crore in 2014-15 to an estimated Rs. 52.08 lakh crore in 2025-26 . Budget allocation for the Department of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare increased from Rs. 27,663 crore in 2013-14 to Rs. 1,40,528.78 crore in 2026 - 27 . Harvesting Higher Production Total foodgrain production increased from 265.05 million tonnes in 2013-14 to 376.56 million tonnes in 2025-26 (Third Advance Estimates). Horticulture production increased from 280.70 million tonnes in 2013-14 to approximately 377.78 million tonnes in 2025-26 (Second Advance Estimates) . Oilseeds production increased from 27.51 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 43.06 million tonnes in 2025-26 ( Third Advance Estimates) . Securing Farmers' Livelihoods Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) More than Rs.4.47 lakh crore has been transferred directly into farmers’ bank accounts through 23 instalments under the Scheme. Under the 23rd instalment, more than 9.49 crore farmers benefited , with over Rs.18,984 crore released. The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) Since its launch in 2016-17, over 92.46 crore farmer applications have been insured. Claims worth Rs.1.96 lakh crore have been disbursed up to December 2025, benefiting around 24.31 crore farmers . Minimum Support Prices (MSP) Total procurement increased from 698.7 million tonnes during 2004-2014 to 1,229.2 million tonnes during 2014-2026. Total MSP value increased from Rs. 7.41 lakh crore during 2004-2014 to Rs. 26.32 lakh crore during 2014- 2026 (up to February 2026). MSP for Paddy (Grade A) increased from Rs.1,400 per quintal in 2014-15 to Rs.2,461 per quintal in 2026-27 . MSP for Wheat increased from Rs.1,400 per quintal in 2014-15 to Rs.2,585 per quintal in 2026-27. The Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme As on 3 rd August 2026, 7.28 crore Kisan Credit Card (KCC) accounts were operational across the country in 2025-26. The amount outstanding under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) scheme stood at Rs. 10.08 lakh crore. The Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PMKMY) As of February 2026, around 24.96 lakh farmers have been enrolled under the scheme. Towards Sustainable Agriculture The Soil Health Card (SHC) Scheme 26.09 crore soil health cards have been issued as of July 2026. ⁠In addition, over 70,002 Krishi Sakhis have been trained to provide soil health advisories and support informed farm practices. Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY) Since its inception (as of June 2026), 18.93 lakh hectares of area have been covered, benefiting 33.63 lakh farmers. Mission Organic Value Chain Development for North Eastern Region (MOVCDNER) Since its inception (as on 30 June 2026), 2.36 lakh hectares have been brought under organic farming benefitting 2.74 lakh farmers. National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) During FY 2025-26, 18,893 clusters covering 10.32 lakh hectares and involving 20.93 lakh farmers were formed under the Mission. 33.89 lakh farmers have been made aware of natural farming. More than 22.47 lakh farmers have been registered under the Natural Farming Certification System (NFCS), of which over 14.43 lakh farmers have been certified. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha Evam Utthan Mahabhiyan (PM KUSUM) As on 2 nd August 2026, Nearly 11.49 lakh off-grid solar pumps have been installed for agricultural use. More than 15.89 lakh agricultural pumps are covered through feeder-level solarisation. Around 1,726 MW of decentralized solar power capacity was commissioned on farmers’ land. Over 21.77 lakh farmers benefited across the country. Ensuring Food for All As of February 2026, under the National Food Security Act (NFSA), against the intended coverage of 81.35 crore , the States/UTs have identified 80.56 crore persons for the provision of subsidized foodgrains. Around 79.8 crore beneficiaries are covered across the country under NFSA, as of December 2025. Centre to spend Rs. 25,530 crore in next 5 years under SARTHAK PDS - Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling-Income with Automation in PDS. The Scheme will work towards fulfilling India's commitment to 81.35 crore persons covered under NFSA. Building Stronger Rural Institutions through Cooperatives and FPO s 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been registered across the country as of July 2026. 79,630 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) have been sanctioned for computerization across 31 States and Union Territories. 63,707 PACS have been onboarded on the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) based national software as of 05th August 2026. Connecting Farms to Markets National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) As of June 2026, 1,656 mandis have been integrated. 1.89 crore farmers and 2.78 lakh traders have been registered on e-NAM. Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) As of July 2026, 12,353 storage infrastructure projects with a storage capacity of 369.18 LMT have been sanctioned in the last ten years. Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Interest subvention support has been extended to 18,893 warehouses, 3,110 cold stores/cold chain projects and 2,105 integrated primary and secondary processing units. Food Processing Reforms Enhanced Financial Support for Food Processing Budget allocation for the Ministry of Food Processing Industries increased from Rs.785.86 crore in 2014-15 to Rs.4,064 crore in 2026-27 . Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) Incentives amounting to Rs. 3,271.44 crore have been disbursed up to June 2026. The investments undertaken under the Scheme have resulted in the creation of food processing capacity of 34 lakh metric tonnes per annum. Sales of PLI-supported products increased from Rs. 58,758 crore in FY 2019-20 to Rs. 1,08,854 crore in FY 2025-26. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) As of June 2026, 1,256 projects (post-harvest infrastructure and processing facilities) have been completed or are operational, benefitting about 37.76 lakh farmers. 294.21 LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity created, generating 9.16 lakh employment opportunities across the country. Taking Indian Agriculture Global The value of agricultural exports increased from USD 32.08 billion in 2014-15 to USD 54.70 billion in 2025-26 , recording a growth of about 70.5 percent . Share of processed food exports increased from 13.7 percent in 2014-15 to 20.4 percent in 2024-25 , a nearly 49 percent rise . Technology at the Farmgate Under the Digital Agriculture Mission As on 3rd August 2026 More than 10.31 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across the country. Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country. AI-Enabled Initiatives: National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS)- As of July 2026, this tool is being used by over 10,000 extension workers supporting 73 crops over 436 pests. BharatVistaar- As of July 2026, the platform has served over 3 lakh farmers and addressed more than 72 lakh farmer queries. Empowering Farmers Through Knowledge Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) As of June 2026, The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has established 731 KVKs across the country. Around 58.02 lakh farmers were trained between 2021-22 and 2023-24. An additional 18.56 lakh farmers were trained during the first ten months of 2024-25. Agricultural Diversification and the Growth of Allied Sectors Livestock and Dairy as Drivers of Rural Economic Growth The livestock sector has recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.77 percent since 2014-15. In the Union Budget 2026-27, Rs. 6,153.46 crore has been allocated to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying . Indigenous and non-descript cattle productivity reached 1,343.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 927 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15. Buffalo productivity reached 2,365.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1880 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15. Average bovine milk productivity has reached 2,251 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1,648 kg per animal per year in 2014-15. India holds the leading global position in milk production , accounting for nearly 25 percent of global output. Per capita milk availability reached 485 grams per day in 2024-25 , compared to the global average of 394 grams per day . Milk production has increased by 70 percent , rising from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 248 million tonnes in 2024-25. Poultry and meat production have also expanded, with India ranking second in egg production and fourth in meat production globally : Egg production has grown by 90 percent , increasing from 78.48 billion eggs in 2014-15 to 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25. Per capita egg availability has risen from 62 eggs per annum in 2014-15 to 106 eggs per annum in 2024-25. Meat Production has increased from 6.69 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 10.50 million tonnes in 2024-25. Strengthening Fisheries Infrastructure, Market Access and Credit Support The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record Rs. 2,761.80 crore to fisheries under the Blue Revolution initiatives. Fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, up from 95.79 lakh tonnes in FY 2013-14. Seafood exports increased from USD 3.64 billion in 2013-14 to around USD 8.46 billion in 2025-26. Fisheries Infrastructure and Market Access Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) Rs. 2,500 crore allocated under the Union Budget 2026-27 . As on April 2026 , Key activities approved: 28,489 fish transportation and handling units 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, and 117 fish retail markets 775 cold storages and ice plants, and 24 wholesale fish markets Institutional Credit Support for fisheries 6.83 lakh applications were received under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) , of which 6.77 lakh were accepted. Of which, 4.82 lakh applications were sanctioned , indicating a meaningful conversion of demand into credit access as of early 2026. KCC benefits have reached 4.39 lakh fishers . Insurance coverage has been provided to 33 lakh beneficiaries. An average of 7.44 lakh fisher families received livelihood assistance during lean fishing periods. Strengthening Livestock through Infrastructure and Entrepreneurship National Livestock Mission As on 4 th August 2026, 4,084 breed multiplication farms for poultry, sheep, goat, pig, camel, horse, and donkey have been approved. 1.61 lakh metric tonnes of quality fodder seed have been produced. Entrepreneurship Development Programme under the National Livestock Mission, as on 11 th August 2026, 4,321 projects approved , worth Rs. 2,948.68 crore total project cost with the Rs. 1,386.18 crore approved subsidy Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) Projects approved with 418 lakh litres/day of milk processing capacity and value-addition capacity as on 4 th August 2026. Bharat Pashudhan As of 6 th August 2026, Livestock Owners Registered: 9.84 crore , Pashu Aadhaar Issued: Over 38.53 crore , All Vaccinations: 168.67 crore . National Programme for Dairy Development ( NPDD) As on June 2026, 36,611 new Dairy Cooperative Societies have been organised. 34,557 village-level dairy cooperative societies have been strengthened. 168 lakh litres/day of milk chilling capacity has been created. 76,748 milk quality testing devices have been distributed. Advancing Livestock Breeding, Productivity, and Animal Health A total of 47,687 Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRIs) have been trained, 24 IVF laboratories established, 48 semen stations sanctioned, and 28 heifer rearing centres approved under RGM as on 4 th August 2026. During the last five years, over 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been carried out under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme , benefiting nearly 5.98 crore farmers . Accelerated Breed Improvement programme : As on 4 th August 2026, 7,959 embryos transferred, 1,666 pregnancies established, and 1,223 calves born. Out of which 1,142 of the calves are females. Strengthening Animal Health and Risk Mitigation Livestock productivity and income stability are closely linked to disease control. Under National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) As of March 2026, 132.49 crore doses of the Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccine have been administered. Brucellosis Control Programme: As of March 2026, 3.17 crores , 4-8 months old bovine female calf for Brucellosis have been vaccinated in the country since inception. 296.74 lakh vaccine doses administered to eligible female calves to prevent brucellosis and strengthen livestock health during the last five years alone. Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) 4,019 MVUs are operational across 29 States/UTs, delivering doorstep veterinary services through the toll-free number 1962 as of July 2026. Benefited 119.77 lakh farmers and treated 245.05 lakh animals , significantly boosting farmer confidence and supporting the livestock sector as a viable enterprise. Centre to spend Rs. 25,530 crore in next 5 years under SARTHAK PDS - Scheme for Assistance in Ration Transport and Handling-Income with Automation in PDS. The Scheme will work towards fulfilling India's commitment to 81.35 crore persons covered under NFSA. Building Stronger Rural Institutions through Cooperatives and FPO s 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) have been registered across the country as of July 2026. 79,630 Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) have been sanctioned for computerization across 31 States and Union Territories. 63,707 PACS have been onboarded on the Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) based national software as of 05th August 2026. Connecting Farms to Markets National Agriculture Market (e-NAM) As of June 2026, 1,656 mandis have been integrated. 1.89 crore farmers and 2.78 lakh traders have been registered on e-NAM. Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) As of July 2026, 12,353 storage infrastructure projects with a storage capacity of 369.18 LMT have been sanctioned in the last ten years. Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) Interest subvention support has been extended to 18,893 warehouses, 3,110 cold stores/cold chain projects and 2,105 integrated primary and secondary processing units. Food Processing Reforms Enhanced Financial Support for Food Processing Budget allocation for the Ministry of Food Processing Industries increased from Rs.785.86 crore in 2014-15 to Rs.4,064 crore in 2026-27 . Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) Incentives amounting to Rs. 3,271.44 crore have been disbursed up to June 2026. The investments undertaken under the Scheme have resulted in the creation of food processing capacity of 34 lakh metric tonnes per annum. Sales of PLI-supported products increased from Rs. 58,758 crore in FY 2019-20 to Rs. 1,08,854 crore in FY 2025-26. Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) As of June 2026, 1,256 projects (post-harvest infrastructure and processing facilities) have been completed or are operational, benefitting about 37.76 lakh farmers. 294.21 LMT/Annum of processing and preservation capacity created, generating 9.16 lakh employment opportunities across the country. Taking Indian Agriculture Global The value of agricultural exports increased from USD 32.08 billion in 2014-15 to USD 54.70 billion in 2025-26 , recording a growth of about 70.5 percent . Share of processed food exports increased from 13.7 percent in 2014-15 to 20.4 percent in 2024-25 , a nearly 49 percent rise . Technology at the Farmgate Under the Digital Agriculture Mission As on 3rd August 2026 More than 10.31 Crore Farmer IDs have been created across the country. Further, during Rabi 2025-26, the Digital Crop Survey (DCS) was conducted in 648 Districts covering more than 31.3 crore plots across the country. AI-Enabled Initiatives: National Pest Surveillance System (NPSS)- As of July 2026, this tool is being used by over 10,000 extension workers supporting 73 crops over 436 pests. BharatVistaar- As of July 2026, the platform has served over 3 lakh farmers and addressed more than 72 lakh farmer queries. Empowering Farmers Through Knowledge Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs) As of June 2026, The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) has established 731 KVKs across the country. Around 58.02 lakh farmers were trained between 2021-22 and 2023-24. An additional 18.56 lakh farmers were trained during the first ten months of 2024-25. Agricultural Diversification and the Growth of Allied Sectors Livestock and Dairy as Drivers of Rural Economic Growth The livestock sector has recorded a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 12.77 percent since 2014-15. In the Union Budget 2026-27, Rs. 6,153.46 crore has been allocated to the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying . Indigenous and non-descript cattle productivity reached 1,343.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 927 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15. Buffalo productivity reached 2,365.2 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1880 kilograms per animal per year in 2014-15. Average bovine milk productivity has reached 2,251 kilograms per animal per year in 2024-25 from 1,648 kg per animal per year in 2014-15. India holds the leading global position in milk production , accounting for nearly 25 percent of global output. Per capita milk availability reached 485 grams per day in 2024-25 , compared to the global average of 394 grams per day . Milk production has increased by 70 percent , rising from 146.31 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 248 million tonnes in 2024-25. Poultry and meat production have also expanded, with India ranking second in egg production and fourth in meat production globally : Egg production has grown by 90 percent , increasing from 78.48 billion eggs in 2014-15 to 149.11 billion eggs in 2024-25. Per capita egg availability has risen from 62 eggs per annum in 2014-15 to 106 eggs per annum in 2024-25. Meat Production has increased from 6.69 million tonnes in 2014-15 to 10.50 million tonnes in 2024-25. Strengthening Fisheries Infrastructure, Market Access and Credit Support The Union Budget 2026-27 allocated a record Rs. 2,761.80 crore to fisheries under the Blue Revolution initiatives. Fish production reached 197.75 lakh tonnes in 2024-25, up from 95.79 lakh tonnes in FY 2013-14. Seafood exports increased from USD 3.64 billion in 2013-14 to around USD 8.46 billion in 2025-26. Fisheries Infrastructure and Market Access Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) Rs. 2,500 crore allocated under the Union Budget 2026-27 . As on April 2026 , Key activities approved: 28,489 fish transportation and handling units 1,394 live fish vending units, 6,018 fish kiosks, and 117 fish retail markets 775 cold storages and ice plants, and 24 wholesale fish markets Institutional Credit Support for fisheries 6.83 lakh applications were received under the Kisan Credit Card (KCC) , of which 6.77 lakh were accepted. Of which, 4.82 lakh applications were sanctioned , indicating a meaningful conversion of demand into credit access as of early 2026. KCC benefits have reached 4.39 lakh fishers . Insurance coverage has been provided to 33 lakh beneficiaries. An average of 7.44 lakh fisher families received livelihood assistance during lean fishing periods. Strengthening Livestock through Infrastructure and Entrepreneurship National Livestock Mission As on 4 th August 2026, 4,084 breed multiplication farms for poultry, sheep, goat, pig, camel, horse, and donkey have been approved. 1.61 lakh metric tonnes of quality fodder seed have been produced. Entrepreneurship Development Programme under the National Livestock Mission, as on 11 th August 2026, 4,321 projects approved , worth Rs. 2,948.68 crore total project cost with the Rs. 1,386.18 crore approved subsidy Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) Projects approved with 418 lakh litres/day of milk processing capacity and value-addition capacity as on 4 th August 2026. Bharat Pashudhan As of 6 th August 2026, Livestock Owners Registered: 9.84 crore , Pashu Aadhaar Issued: Over 38.53 crore , All Vaccinations: 168.67 crore . National Programme for Dairy Development ( NPDD) As on June 2026, 36,611 new Dairy Cooperative Societies have been organised. 34,557 village-level dairy cooperative societies have been strengthened. 168 lakh litres/day of milk chilling capacity has been created. 76,748 milk quality testing devices have been distributed. Advancing Livestock Breeding, Productivity, and Animal Health A total of 47,687 Multi-Purpose Artificial Insemination Technicians in Rural India (MAITRIs) have been trained, 24 IVF laboratories established, 48 semen stations sanctioned, and 28 heifer rearing centres approved under RGM as on 4 th August 2026. During the last five years, over 17.27 crore artificial inseminations have been carried out under the Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme , benefiting nearly 5.98 crore farmers . Accelerated Breed Improvement programme : As on 4 th August 2026, 7,959 embryos transferred, 1,666 pregnancies established, and 1,223 calves born. Out of which 1,142 of the calves are females. Strengthening Animal Health and Risk Mitigation Livestock productivity and income stability are closely linked to disease control. Under National Animal Disease Control Programme (NADCP) As of March 2026, 132.49 crore doses of the Foot and Mouth Disease (FMD) vaccine have been administered. Brucellosis Control Programme: As of March 2026, 3.17 crores , 4-8 months old bovine female calf for Brucellosis have been vaccinated in the country since inception. 296.74 lakh vaccine doses administered to eligible female calves to prevent brucellosis and strengthen livestock health during the last five years alone. Mobile Veterinary Units (MVUs) 4,019 MVUs are operational across 29 States/UTs, delivering doorstep veterinary services through the toll-free number 1962 as of July 2026. Benefited 119.77 lakh farmers and treated 245.05 lakh animals , significantly boosting farmer confidence and supporting the livestock sector as a viable enterprise. title: Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Affordable and Accessible Healthcare for All प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 5:11PM by PIB Delhi In past 12 years, the Government of India has significantly strengthened India’s health system. Quality healthcare is more accessible, more affordable, and more equitable than it has ever been.  This aligns with the principle of “Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas and Sabka Prayas” to build an Atmanirbhar Bharat. Ayushman Bharat T he Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) provides health insurance of Rs. 5 lakh per family per year to families from the poorest 40% of society and all senior citizens aged 70 and above . Over 40,000 claims are processed every single day for over 1,900 treatment packages. Since the scheme launched in 2018, as of August 12, 2026: Over 45.5 crore Ayushman Cards have been issued 12.69 crore hospitalizations have been covered, amounting to Rs. 1.92 lakh crore (as on June 30, 2026) Over 38,466 public and private hospitals are empanelled 1.20 crore senior citizens enrolled under the Ayushman Bharat Vay Vandana scheme. Over 13.84 lakh treatments, worth Rs. 3,000-crore have been availed. Under AB PM-JAY, 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 8,383.97 crore, have been authorised (as on June 30, 2026) Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) are now functional across the country to provide primary healthcare at every neighbourhood (As of 12 August 2026). These centres offer 12 free services and have recorded a cumulative footfall of over 540 crore till date . The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) : Support for 23,224 rural health and wellness centres in 10 high-focus states. Establishing 13,736 urban health and wellness centres in all states. 3,389 block public health units in 11 high-focus states. Setting up 744 integrated public health labs in all districts. Establishing 631 critical care hospital blocks in all districts with a population of more than 5 lakh. And underpinning all of this is India’s digital health backbone, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). Coverage under ABDM (as of August 12, 2026): 96.43 crore ABHA health identity numbers created Over 110 crore health records have been linked with ABHA Over 5.47 lakh health facilities have been registered on the platform More than 10.50 lakh healthcare professionals have been registered on the platform. National Health Mission: Targeted Health Interventions The National Health Mission (NHM), with its two sub-missions- National Rural Health Mission and National Urban Health Mission , delivers targeted programmes that address specific diseases, populations, and health challenges. NHM has significantly improved public health outcomes across maternal and child health, disease elimination, and immunisation. Maternal and Child Health: Making Safe Births the Norm The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan has enabled over 7.91 crore free antenatal check-ups . More than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified. First-trimester antenatal registration in India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). On immunisation, the Universal Immunisation Programme reaches 2.67 crore newborns and 2.9 crore pregnant women every year with free vaccines against 12 diseases. Mission Indradhanush , launched in 2014, has functioned as a catch-up drive, vaccinating 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women across its various phases. The percentage of zero-dose children-those who had received no vaccines at all-dropped from 0.11% of the population in 2023 to 0.06% in 2024 . Under Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), the government launched U-WIN in October 2024 — a platform that ensures no family loses its vaccination records. As of March 2026, 11.87 crore children and 3.96 crore pregnant women are already registered. In February 2026, the government launched a three-month campaign to provide free HPV vaccines to 1.2 crore girls aged 14 years, for combating cervical cancer. 52,10,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine across the country (as on July 15, 2026). These initiatives have improved various mortality rates, including: Maternal mortality rate declined to 87 per 1,00,000 live births in 2022-24 from 130 per 1,00,000 in 2014-16 . Neonatal mortality rate declined to 17 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 28 per 1,000 live births in 2015. Under-5 mortality rate declined to 28 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 48 per 1,000 live births in 2015 . Eliminating Communicable Diseases: Real Progress on Long-Standing Burdens The government has reduced the prevalence of communicable diseases over the past 12 years. New cases of tuberculosis emerging yearly in India dipped by 21% from 2015-2024; mortality due to TB dropped by 28% during the same period . Treatment success rates in Tuberculosis have climbed from 83% in 2021 to 90% in 2025 — and treatment coverage has gone from 53% (2015) to 92% (2024). More than 28.1 crore people have already been screened , 20 Lakh people given preventive treatment, and 5.7 lakh new Nikshay Mitras have been added so far under the intensified campaigns since December 2024. Malaria cases and deaths have fallen by 80.5% and 78.38% respectively between 2015 and 2023 . India exited the WHO's 'High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group' for malaria in 2024. Non-Communicable Diseases: Catching Problems Early National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, screening, early diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). Through nationwide screening drives: 41.5 crore Screened for hypertension 41.3 crore for diabetes 35.3 crore for oral cancer and 16.5 crore for breast cancer. The Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (launched 2016) has provided free dialysis to 32.44 lakh patients across 1,856 centres (as of June, 2026). Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Cancer Care Centres Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes (SCIs) and 20 Tertiary Cancer Care Centers (TCCCs) have been approved . Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres (DCCCs) and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country. India has achieved a 17.3% relative reduction in overall tobacco use from 2009-10 to 2016-17, as per the Report of the second round of the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS- 2). To achieve a tobacco-free generation, the Government launched the Tobacco Free Youth Campaign in 2023 — now in its third edition. This work has earned India the 2025 Bloomberg Philanthropies Award for tobacco control. Making Medicines and Tests Actually Affordable The Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has made generic medicines cheaper. The Jan Aushadhi Kendras, where these medicines are available, have grown from a handful of stores in 2014-15 to over 18,646 Jan Aushadhi Kendras as of February 2026. These medicines are sold at 50–80% below branded prices , with a basket of over 2,000 medicines and 300 surgical devices . AMRIT (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) Pharmacies launched in 2015, go even further, offering life-saving medicines at discounts of 50–90% , making treatment affordable for low-income patients who would otherwise go without treatment. The scheme has benefited more than 6.85 crore patients and medicines worth over Rs. 17,000 crore at MRP have been dispensed so far, resulting in cumulative savings of about Rs. 8,400 crore for patients. Free Diagnostics Service Initiative under NHM makes tests, X-rays, blood work free at every level of the public health system from sub-centres all the way up to district hospitals, spanning haematology, radiology, biochemistry, and more. Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities 14 tests at Sub Centers 63 at Primary Health Centers 97 at Community Health Centres 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals 134 tests at District Hospitals. Reaching People Where They Are: Digital Health and Telemedicine eSanjeevani , India's national telemedicine platform, has delivered over 49 crore consultations since its launch in 2019 (as on August 11, 2026). Over 2.4 lakh healthcare providers are now on the platform. Tele-MANAS — launched in October 2022 — was introduced as a toll-free helpline (14416) available nationwide, offering a wide range of mental health services. It operates in 20 languages across all 36 states and union territories. It has already received 43.64 lakh calls since the launch of the service, through 53 Tele-Manas Cells and 23 Mentoring Institutes (as on August 11, 2026). i-DRONE service launched in 2021 is delivering medicines and vaccines by drone. 22,000 medicines have been delivered over 7,700 kilometres through 65 healthcare centres. AI is now also embedded in care delivery. Between April 2023 and November 2025, 28.2 crore eSanjeevani consultations were supported by AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems, providing real-time clinical alerts to doctors. Building the Workforce India Needs Over the past 12 years, the number of medical colleges has more than doubled — from 387 to 818 allopathy colleges (as of 2025-2026) . 12 new AIIMS have been made functional since 2014. There are 23 AIIMS now. MBBS and PG seats increased to 1,28,976 and 85,822, respectively, as of 2025-26. Nursing has received equal attention. 157 new nursing colleges are being set up, adding around 15,700 nursing graduates annually . B.Sc. Nursing seats are up 53% to 1,27,290, and M.Sc. Nursing seats up 39% to 14,986 as of June 2025. Alternative Healthcare Alongside modern medicine, the government has formally integrated traditional healthcare systems into the public health framework. The Ministry of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa, and Homeopathy), formed in November 2014, has established traditional medicines as an active part of India's health system. 942 AYUSH institutions exist in the country as of May 2025. Ayush Grid is India’s digital bridge between traditional healing and modern healthcare delivery, making AYUSH more accessible, integrated, and future-ready. This AYUSH Grid will digitally connect all AYUSH hospitals and laboratories nationwide. Under AB PM-JAY, 29.05 lakh inter-state portability hospital admissions, amounting to more than Rs. 8,383.97 crore, have been authorised (as on June 30, 2026) Over 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs (AAMs) are now functional across the country to provide primary healthcare at every neighbourhood (As of 12 August 2026). These centres offer 12 free services and have recorded a cumulative footfall of over 540 crore till date . The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) : Support for 23,224 rural health and wellness centres in 10 high-focus states. Establishing 13,736 urban health and wellness centres in all states. 3,389 block public health units in 11 high-focus states. Setting up 744 integrated public health labs in all districts. Establishing 631 critical care hospital blocks in all districts with a population of more than 5 lakh. And underpinning all of this is India’s digital health backbone, the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM). Coverage under ABDM (as of August 12, 2026): 96.43 crore ABHA health identity numbers created Over 110 crore health records have been linked with ABHA Over 5.47 lakh health facilities have been registered on the platform More than 10.50 lakh healthcare professionals have been registered on the platform. National Health Mission: Targeted Health Interventions The National Health Mission (NHM), with its two sub-missions- National Rural Health Mission and National Urban Health Mission , delivers targeted programmes that address specific diseases, populations, and health challenges. NHM has significantly improved public health outcomes across maternal and child health, disease elimination, and immunisation. Maternal and Child Health: Making Safe Births the Norm The Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan has enabled over 7.91 crore free antenatal check-ups . More than 1.24 crore high-risk pregnancies have been identified. First-trimester antenatal registration in India increased from 58.6% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 76.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Mothers receiving four or more antenatal care visits in India increased significantly from 51.2% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 65.2% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). Institutional deliveries in India increased from 78.9% in NFHS-4 (2015-16) to 90.6% in NFHS-6 (2023-24). On immunisation, the Universal Immunisation Programme reaches 2.67 crore newborns and 2.9 crore pregnant women every year with free vaccines against 12 diseases. Mission Indradhanush , launched in 2014, has functioned as a catch-up drive, vaccinating 5.46 crore children and 1.32 crore pregnant women across its various phases. The percentage of zero-dose children-those who had received no vaccines at all-dropped from 0.11% of the population in 2023 to 0.06% in 2024 . Under Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP), the government launched U-WIN in October 2024 — a platform that ensures no family loses its vaccination records. As of March 2026, 11.87 crore children and 3.96 crore pregnant women are already registered. In February 2026, the government launched a three-month campaign to provide free HPV vaccines to 1.2 crore girls aged 14 years, for combating cervical cancer. 52,10,302 girls have received the HPV vaccine across the country (as on July 15, 2026). These initiatives have improved various mortality rates, including: Maternal mortality rate declined to 87 per 1,00,000 live births in 2022-24 from 130 per 1,00,000 in 2014-16 . Neonatal mortality rate declined to 17 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 28 per 1,000 live births in 2015. Under-5 mortality rate declined to 28 per 1,000 live births in 2023 from 48 per 1,000 live births in 2015 . Eliminating Communicable Diseases: Real Progress on Long-Standing Burdens The government has reduced the prevalence of communicable diseases over the past 12 years. New cases of tuberculosis emerging yearly in India dipped by 21% from 2015-2024; mortality due to TB dropped by 28% during the same period . Treatment success rates in Tuberculosis have climbed from 83% in 2021 to 90% in 2025 — and treatment coverage has gone from 53% (2015) to 92% (2024). More than 28.1 crore people have already been screened , 20 Lakh people given preventive treatment, and 5.7 lakh new Nikshay Mitras have been added so far under the intensified campaigns since December 2024. Malaria cases and deaths have fallen by 80.5% and 78.38% respectively between 2015 and 2023 . India exited the WHO's 'High Burden to High Impact (HBHI) group' for malaria in 2024. Non-Communicable Diseases: Catching Problems Early National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases (NP-NCD) focuses on strengthening infrastructure, human resource development, screening, early diagnosis, referral, treatment, and health promotion for Non-Communicable Diseases (NCDs). Through nationwide screening drives: 41.5 crore Screened for hypertension 41.3 crore for diabetes 35.3 crore for oral cancer and 16.5 crore for breast cancer. The Pradhan Mantri National Dialysis Programme (launched 2016) has provided free dialysis to 32.44 lakh patients across 1,856 centres (as of June, 2026). Under the Strengthening of Tertiary Cancer Care Centres Facilities Scheme, 19 State Cancer Institutes (SCIs) and 20 Tertiary Cancer Care Centers (TCCCs) have been approved . Under the National Programme for Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases, 770 District NCD Clinics, 524 Day Care Cancer Centres (DCCCs) and 6,410 NCD clinics at Community Health Centres have been set up across the country. India has achieved a 17.3% relative reduction in overall tobacco use from 2009-10 to 2016-17, as per the Report of the second round of the Global Adult Tobacco Survey (GATS- 2). To achieve a tobacco-free generation, the Government launched the Tobacco Free Youth Campaign in 2023 — now in its third edition. This work has earned India the 2025 Bloomberg Philanthropies Award for tobacco control. Making Medicines and Tests Actually Affordable The Pradhan Mantri Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP) has made generic medicines cheaper. The Jan Aushadhi Kendras, where these medicines are available, have grown from a handful of stores in 2014-15 to over 18,646 Jan Aushadhi Kendras as of February 2026. These medicines are sold at 50–80% below branded prices , with a basket of over 2,000 medicines and 300 surgical devices . AMRIT (Affordable Medicines and Reliable Implants for Treatment) Pharmacies launched in 2015, go even further, offering life-saving medicines at discounts of 50–90% , making treatment affordable for low-income patients who would otherwise go without treatment. The scheme has benefited more than 6.85 crore patients and medicines worth over Rs. 17,000 crore at MRP have been dispensed so far, resulting in cumulative savings of about Rs. 8,400 crore for patients. Free Diagnostics Service Initiative under NHM makes tests, X-rays, blood work free at every level of the public health system from sub-centres all the way up to district hospitals, spanning haematology, radiology, biochemistry, and more. Diagnostics services are provided free of cost at all levels of public health facilities 14 tests at Sub Centers 63 at Primary Health Centers 97 at Community Health Centres 111 tests at Sub District Hospitals 134 tests at District Hospitals. Reaching People Where They Are: Digital Health and Telemedicine eSanjeevani , India's national telemedicine platform, has delivered over 49 crore consultations since its launch in 2019 (as on August 11, 2026). Over 2.4 lakh healthcare providers are now on the platform. Tele-MANAS — launched in October 2022 — was introduced as a toll-free helpline (14416) available nationwide, offering a wide range of mental health services. It operates in 20 languages across all 36 states and union territories. It has already received 43.64 lakh calls since the launch of the service, through 53 Tele-Manas Cells and 23 Mentoring Institutes (as on August 11, 2026). i-DRONE service launched in 2021 is delivering medicines and vaccines by drone. 22,000 medicines have been delivered over 7,700 kilometres through 65 healthcare centres. AI is now also embedded in care delivery. Between April 2023 and November 2025, 28.2 crore eSanjeevani consultations were supported by AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support Systems, providing real-time clinical alerts to doctors. Building the Workforce India Needs Over the past 12 years, the number of medical colleges has more than doubled — from 387 to 818 allopathy colleges (as of 2025-2026) . 12 new AIIMS have been made functional since 2014. There are 23 AIIMS now. MBBS and PG seats increased to 1,28,976 and 85,822, respectively, as of 2025-26. Nursing has received equal attention. 157 new nursing colleges are being set up, adding around 15,700 nursing graduates annually . B.Sc. Nursing seats are up 53% to 1,27,290, and M.Sc. Nursing seats up 39% to 14,986 as of June 2025. Alternative Healthcare Alongside modern medicine, the government has formally integrated traditional healthcare systems into the public health framework. The Ministry of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Sowa Rigpa, and Homeopathy), formed in November 2014, has established traditional medicines as an active part of India's health system. 942 AYUSH institutions exist in the country as of May 2025. Ayush Grid is India’s digital bridge between traditional healing and modern healthcare delivery, making AYUSH more accessible, integrated, and future-ready. This AYUSH Grid will digitally connect all AYUSH hospitals and laboratories nationwide. title: Financial Inclusion in India: Banking Every Citizen, Empowering Every Household
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau PIB Backgrounder Financial Inclusion in India: Banking Every Citizen, Empowering Every Household प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                12 AUG 2026 4:16PM by PIB Delhi Introduction Financial inclusion is central to India's vision of equitable development. Over the past decade, India has expanded access to banking, digital payments, credit, insurance, pensions and investment opportunities. Digital Public Infrastructure and citizen-centric reforms have driven this transformation. India has moved beyond universal bank account ownership towards active participation in the formal financial system. This transformation has empowered millions of households, entrepreneurs and businesses. Key Indicators of Financial Inclusion in India Several indicators highlight the significant progress made in expanding financial access, infrastructure and participation across India. RBI's Financial Inclusion (FI) Index The RBI's FI Index measures the extent of financial inclusion across access, usage and quality of financial services. It serves as a comprehensive indicator of progress in expanding formal financial services nationwide. The FI Index increased from 43.4 in March 2017 to 70.0 in March 2026 , reflecting broad-based improvements across all three dimensions. World Bank Global Findex The Global Findex Database is the world's leading source of data on financial inclusion. It measures how adults access and use financial services across economies. The Global Findex 2025 highlights India's remarkable progress in financial inclusion. Account ownership has reached 89% since 2011, reflecting significant gains in access to formal financial services and active account usage over the past decade. Banking Access Network Bank branches remain the foundation of India's formal banking system. They provide savings, credit and other financial services across the country. India has over 1.81 lakh bank branches (17 July 2026). Banking access is delivered through branches, Business Correspondents and India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) outlets. As of 6 March 2026 , 99.92% villages in the country are covered with banking outlets within a 5 km radius. IPPB strengthens last-mile banking through over 1.65 lakh post offices (17 July, 2026). It serves more than 11 crore customers across 5.57 lakh villages and towns . Business Correspondents extend doorstep banking services to unbanked and under-banked areas. India has over 17.36 lakh BC supporting doorstep banking services nationwide (17 July 2026). Pillars of Financial Inclusion India's financial inclusion ecosystem rests on interconnected policy and institutional pillars. They promote universal access and meaningful participation in the formal financial system. Universal Banking Pradhan Mantri Jan - Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) PMJDY (2014) provides every unbanked adult with a basic savings bank account where minimum balance needs to be maintained. It offers access to savings, remittances, credit, insurance, pension and Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT). PMJDY account holders are provided a RuPay Debit Card and accident insurance cover. The insurance cover is ₹2 lakh for accounts opened after 28 August 2018 and ₹1 lakh for accounts opened before that date. Eligible account holders can also avail an overdraft facility up to ₹10,000. It facilitates enrolment under Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY), Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY), Atal Pension Yojana (APY), and access to MUDRA loans. JAM Trinity The JAM Trinity Integrates Jan Dhan accounts, Aadhaar and mobile connectivity to strengthen financial inclusion. It enables Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) for transparent and efficient delivery of government benefits. DBT reduces leakages, eliminates fake beneficiaries and minimises intermediaries in welfare delivery. The JAM Trinity strengthens formal banking access and promotes trust in digital financial services. Total Direct Benefit Transfer No. of Schemes No. of Ministries Involved (as on 10 August, 2026) ₹ 52,89,019 Cr 320 56 Social Security for All Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) PMJJBY (2015) is an annual renewable life insurance scheme which offers a ₹2 lakh life cover for individuals aged 18–50 years. The scheme is available at an annual premium of ₹436 , which is auto-debited from the subscriber's bank account. It provides financial security to families in the event of the insured person's death. The scheme provides immediate cover for accidental death and a 30-day waiting period for non-accidental death. Gross Enrolments No. of Claim Received No. of Claims Disbursed (as on 30 June 2026) 27.78 Cr 11,31,505 10,97,751 Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) PMSBY (2015) is also an annual renewable accident insurance scheme for savings bank account holders aged 18–70 years. It provides ₹2 lakh cover for accidental death or full disability, and ₹1 lakh for partial disability. The insurance is available at an annual premium of ₹20 which is auto-debited from the linked bank account. Gross Enrolments No. of Claim Received No. of Claims Disbursed (as on 30 June 2026) 58.66 Cr 2,56,526 1,89,057 Atal Pension Yojana (APY) APY (2015) is a contributory pension scheme for workers in the unorganised sector , launched in 2015. It provides a guaranteed monthly pension ranging from ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after attaining 60 years of age. The contributions are based on the subscriber's age at enrolment and the chosen pension amount. Enrolment under the scheme is facilitated through banks and post offices, expanding pension coverage among low-income workers. Total Subscribers Male Subscribers Female Subscribers Transgender Subscribers (as on 30 June 2026) 9.29 crore 4.72 crore (50.8%) 4.56 crore (49.16%) 26,599 (0.028%) Inclusive Credit PM Mudra Yojana PM Mudra Yojana (2015) provides collateral-free loans up to ₹20 lakh to non-corporate, non-farm micro and small enterprises across manufacturing, trading, services, and allied agricultural activities . Mudra loans are extended for a wide range of activities that promote income generation and employment creation. It offers four loan categories based on enterprise growth: Shishu, Kishor, Tarun and Tarun Plus. Total No. of Accounts Amount Sanctioned Amount Disbursed (as on 31 March 2026) 4.48 crore ₹ 5.65 lakh crore ₹ 5.54 lakh crore PM SVANidhi PM SVANidhi is a first-of-its-kind micro-credit initiative focused on street vendors with government-backed credit guarantee support. It provides collateral-free loans in three progressive tranches of ₹15,000, ₹25,000 and ₹50,000. The scheme offers interest subsidy and credit guarantee support to eligible street vendors. Total Beneficiaries Loans Disbursed Total Loan Value (as on May 2026) More than 75.5 lakh Over 1.12 crore More than ₹17,800 crore Kisan Credit Card (KCC) KCC provides timely and adequate credit to farmers through the banking system . It offers an ATM-enabled debit card, one-time documentation and flexible withdrawals. KCC provides credit for crop cultivation, post-harvest needs, marketing, farm maintenance, household expenses and allied activities. Total number of KCC/ISS applications (as on 10 August 2026) Commercial Bank Rural Bank Cooperative Bank 763.6 lakh 368.6 Lakh 1242.0 Lakh Jan Samarth Jan Samarth is a unified digital platform for credit-linked government schemes . It connects beneficiaries directly with lenders, simplifying access to government-sponsored credit. The platform has 16 registered credit schemes, 8 loan categories and more than 300 lenders. No. of Applications Amount of Applications (as on 1 June 2026) 54.10 lakh ₹ 3,00,951 crore Digital Financial Inclusion UPI UPI has emerged as the backbone of India's digital payments ecosystem , driving financial inclusion and digital transactions. The transaction volume increased nearly 12,000-fold and transaction value increased nearly 4,000-fold between FY 2016–17 and FY 2025–26. The IMF has recognised UPI as the world's largest real-time payment system by transaction volume, highlighting India's digital public infrastructure leadership. Volume of Transactions Value of Transactions No. of Banks live on UPI (as on July 2026) 2,365.8 crore 29,87,880.49 crore 741 Financial Literacy National Centre for Financial Education (NCFE) The centre promotes financial education and awareness across all sections of society under the National Strategy for Financial Education. It conducts seminars, workshops, training programmes and awareness campaigns to strengthen financial literacy. It also develops targeted financial education materials covering financial markets and digital financial services Workshops Conducted Beneficiaries Male Female (as on 10 August, 2026) 31,082 10,68,571 373,999 (35%) 694,572 (65%) Financial Education Programme for Adults (FEPA) FEPA was launched in September 2019 by NCFE to promote financial awareness among adults. The programme covers farmers, women’s groups, ASHA and Anganwadi workers, SHGs, employees and skill development trainees. It focuses on Special Focused Districts (SFDs), aligned with the National Strategy for Financial Education. Workshops Conducted Beneficiaries Covered (as on 10 August, 2026) 19,266 6,48,512 Nationwide Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign The four-month campaign was launched on 1 July, 2025 to extend financial inclusion across 2.70 lakh Gram Panchayats and ULBs. More than 2.67 lakh camps were organised across villages and towns during the campaign. 5.19 crore KYC re-verifications, 1.20 crore nomination updates were completed and 92,066 claims were settled under PMJJBY/ PMSBY PMJDY accounts Opened PMJJBY Enrolments PMSBY Enrolments APY Enrolments (as on 31st October 2025) 1.11 crore 1.40 crore 2.86 crore 44.43 lakh From Access to Empowerment India's financial inclusion journey has evolved from expanding account ownership to enabling meaningful financial participation. A strong network of banks, digital infrastructure and government schemes has widened access to formal financial services. PMJDY, JAM trinity, social security and inclusive credit have strengthened financial resilience across diverse sections of society.  Digital payments and financial literacy are further enabling citizens to participate confidently in the formal financial system. Together, these initiatives are building a more accessible, resilient and inclusive financial ecosystem that supports inclusive growth.
